In the Curie–Weiss limit, for couplings below the equilibrium threshold, shortening the readout interval drives a continuous transition to an ordered stationary state even though the programmed Boltzmann distribution remains disordered.

entry.title: Quantum States and Spectra of Small Cylindrical and Toroidal Lattices
entry.summary: Quantum States and Spectra of Small Cylindrical and Toroidal Lattices arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the spectra and quantum states of small cylindrical and toroidal lattices under a scalar gauge potential that adds a position-dependent phase to inter-site coupling. Periodic boundary conditions generally break the gauge equivalence assumed for infinite lattices, and the authors identify conditions that restore it. They report gauge-dependent avoided crossings and persistent degeneracies, and examine the effects of boundary conditions, coupling strengths, and an axial field.

entry.title: Block-wise quantum algorithm for PDEs with interface penalties
entry.summary: Block-Wise Variational Quantum Algorithms for PDEs with Interface Penalty Constraints arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes a block-wise variational quantum algorithm for solving partial differential equations whose solutions vary in complexity across space. The domain is split into local quantum subproblems, with grid sizes and circuit designs assigned according to a computable difficulty indicator. Neighboring blocks are coupled through jump penalties on state values, derivatives, and fluxes, and the rough regions are adaptively tracked. Simulations on elliptic, advection-diffusion, and Burgers problems show lower errors and smaller peak local circuit width than global variational quantum approaches.

entry.title: Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction for Benzene Dimer Stacking Energies
entry.summary: A Divide-and-Conquer Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction for Evaluating π-π Stacking Interaction Energies in the Benzene Dimer arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes Divide-and-Conquer Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction (Deep QSCI) to evaluate π-π stacking interaction energies in the sandwich benzene dimer. QSCI is run on one monomer, and a reduced local basis built from its ground state is used to diagonalize an effective dimer Hamiltonian, reusing monomer results across monomers and distances to cut the required qubits from 40 to 20. With 6-31G**, the minimum is -0.91 kcal/mol at 4.0 Å, compared with -1.14 kcal/mol from counterpoise-corrected CCSD(T). With cc-pVDZ, large cancellations appear, which the authors suggest may stem from insufficient consistency of active orbitals and local bases between monomers.

entry.title: Optimizing randomized quantum simulation of Hamiltonians by minimizing average error
entry.summary: Optimized Randomized Hamiltonian Simulation via Average-Error Analysis arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper presents a framework for randomized Hamiltonian simulation that samples terms with arbitrary probabilities and implements their short-time evolutions in sequence. It shows that sampling in proportion to Hilbert-Schmidt norms, derived from Haar-averaged error bounds, can give smaller average-error bounds than the standard qDRIFT method. For Pauli-string Hamiltonians, combining this with commuting Pauli grouping further reduces error bounds at fixed depth.

entry.title: Single-photon nonlinearity from a quantum dot in a nanobeam cavity
entry.summary: Single-Photon Nonlinearity from a Nanobeam with a Quantum Dot arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper reports a single-photon nonlinearity built from a nanobeam cavity coupled to one quantum dot. The device couples directly to a single-mode fiber with 60% efficiency and reaches the nonlinearity at a threshold of 0.24 incident photons per resonant picosecond pulse. The system operates in the strong-coupling regime, with a coupling rate g/2π of 29.1 GHz and cooperativity C of 3.98. The authors present it as a compact, chip-integrable, fiber-compatible building block for photonic quantum technologies.

entry.title: Synchronizing quantum devices over lossy channels using polarization assistance
entry.summary: Synchronized Quantum Devices in Lossy Channels arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a polarization-assisted protocol that uses entangled photon pairs to keep quantum devices synchronized under high channel loss, such as satellite-to-ground links. The experiments show reliable synchronization at higher losses and up to a 40% increase in satellite-to-ground distance. Monte Carlo simulations indicate the improvement holds across a wide range of photon-starved conditions.

entry.title: Root-system structure of sloppiness in passive Gaussian metrology
entry.summary: Root-system structure of sloppiness in passive Gaussian metrology arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies when passive transformations of squeezed Gaussian probes become locally unidentifiable because the quantum Fisher matrix loses rank. It shows that the C_n restricted-root system of Sp(2n,R)/U(n) governs this exact sloppiness for pure zero-mean Gaussian probes. It also solves the E-optimal probe-design problem of maximizing the smallest passive Fisher eigenvalue at fixed mean photon number.

entry.title: Shared phase arithmetic: applying a layer of diagonal quantum rotations at once
entry.summary: Shared Phase Arithmetic for Parallel Quantum Rotations arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proposes parallel phase kickback (PPK), which coherently computes a weighted sum of several rotation parameters, adds it once to a phase-gradient state, and then uncomputes it. This separates the cost of representing a phase function from the cost of applying it. The authors prove correctness, give explicit error bounds, and analyze logical gate counts for general weights, pairs of rotations, and weights with disjoint binary support. The bounds show when shared phase arithmetic reduces amortized rotation cost and when encoding overhead limits that advantage.

entry.title: A paper on how quantum Fisher information and quantum coherence factorize over time
entry.summary: Factorization dynamics between quantum Fisher information and quantum coherence arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the factorization relationship between quantum Fisher information, which measures how sensitive a quantum state is to parameter changes, and quantum coherence. The authors prepared pure states in qubit and qutrit systems, applied unitary evolution, and confirmed the factorization law both theoretically and experimentally. They also derived a lower bound on the variance of the estimated parameter that does not require final-state information.

entry.title: A general spin-chain method for multicomponent anyons in 1D optical lattices
entry.summary: Generalized Effective Spin-Chain formalism for multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces a generalized effective spin-chain (GESC) framework for strongly interacting multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices. It maps particle motion to spinless fermions and spin states to an ordered chain, separating spin and charge degrees of freedom. The authors report that in the strong-interaction regime the fractional exchange phase appears in spin-exchange coefficients through virtual tunneling. They also describe how direction-dependent phases affect non-equilibrium impurity transport.

entry.title: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices: a study of how particles with fractional exchange statistics behave in a 1D lattice
entry.summary: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the ground-state and dynamical behavior of multicomponent interacting anyons confined in a one-dimensional optical lattice, using the Anyon-Hubbard model. It shows that fractional exchange statistics combined with multicomponent effects reshape charge and spin correlations, including asymmetric momentum-distribution shells and new peaks. The authors report antiferromagnetic spin ordering and find that the statistical phase parameter can switch dipole oscillations between underdamped and overdamped regimes.

entry.title: Emergent symmetries after ensemble averaging: a review of how global symmetries can arise in quantum gravity.
entry.summary: Emergent Symmetries in Ensemble Averages arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper reviews work showing that global symmetries, believed absent in quantum gravity, can emerge after ensemble averages of theories as encountered in holography. Its case study is the ensemble average of two-dimensional Narain-type conformal field theories with an even quadratic form, computed by the Siegel-Weil formula and interpreted as a sum over geometries in a three-dimensional Abelian Chern-Simons theory. The authors also relate this to the Swampland program and recast strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking of mixed states as symmetry emergence in ensemble averages, motivating a new Swampland conjecture.

entry.title: Quantum References Beat Classical Ones for Leakage Detection
entry.summary: Exponential Advantage of Quantum over Classical References in Leakage Detection arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper shows that leakage from an encoding subspace can be detected using independent quantum reference states prepared by the same encoder, without a classical description of the encoding. For orthogonal leakage, the miss probability is asymptotically 4/M, independent of the ambient dimension. Measuring all references first yields zero detection under the same zero-false-alarm requirement. For one logical qubit in three physical qubits, seven coherent references achieve at least 50% detection, while a measurement-first receiver needs at least 588. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes detecting leakage with independent quantum references from the same encoder, needing no classical encoding description; the authors prove optimality under zero false alarm and report that for

entry.title: Factorization of driven anisotropic Rabi–Stark Hamiltonians via affine spin pencils
entry.summary: Affine spin-pencil factorization of generalized driven anisotropic Rabi--Stark Hamiltonians in an inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper constructs a supersymmetric factorization of generalized driven anisotropic Rabi–Stark Hamiltonians using an affine factor in an inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra. The normal product has an exact zero-energy ground doublet and a Witten index of two. It also covers a Bargmann hierarchy, endpoint conditions for exceptional finite-polynomial states, several limiting cases, and an interior example with additional drives, Stark deformation and intensity-dependent coupling.

entry.title: Evanescent-wave Johnson noise from superconductors, explained
entry.summary: Evanescent-wave Johnson Noise from Superconductors arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper calculates evanescent-wave Johnson noise above a superconductor's surface and the resulting relaxation time T1 of spin and charge qubits placed nanometers away. It uses a microscopic current-response kernel for a BCS superconductor, together with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and nonlocal surface impedances. Magnetic noise is enhanced just below Tc by the coherence peak and falls exponentially at lower temperatures, while magnetic impurities produce a zero-temperature noise floor. ★★★★ Notable: Presents a theory of evanescent-wave Johnson noise and near-surface qubit T1 above superconductors, predicting a magnetic-noise coherence peak below Tc, a zero-temperature noise floor from magnetic im

entry.title: How work cumulants scale when a driven Gaussian field crosses over between regimes
entry.summary: Crossover of Scaling Behaviors of Work Cumulants in a Driven Gaussian Field Theory arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper derives the finite-temperature characteristic function of work for a driven O(N) Gaussian field theory and gives closed-form expressions for all zero-temperature excess-work cumulants. For gapped protocols, adiabatic perturbation theory yields a τ_Q^-2 scaling, where τ_Q is the protocol duration. For power-law protocols approaching criticality, the authors analyze the competition between critical excitations and regular contributions, identifying Kibble–Zurek-type scaling and a logarithmic correction at a specific threshold.

entry.title: Dynamical resource theory of time-reversal symmetry breaking
entry.summary: Dynamical resource theory of time-reversal symmetry breaking arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proposes an operationally meaningful framework for quantifying the intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking (T-violation) of quantum channels, treating it as a resource within dynamical resource theory. T-violation is split into kinematic T-violation, arising from antiunitary motion-reversal, and nonunitality driven purely by thermodynamics. The authors also analyze the resulting resource theory of kinematic T-violation and report a universal golden unit, including for classical channels.

entry.title: Puncturing method for adaptive entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes
entry.summary: Puncturing for Adaptive Entanglement-Assisted Stabilizer Codes arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper extends a puncturing construction for standard stabilizer codes to entanglement-assisted codes, so that one mother code can be adjusted to different numbers of available pre-shared Bell pairs. The three-step procedure treats the code as unassisted, punctures one receiver-side qubit, and recovers an entanglement-assisted form, reducing the required Bell pairs by one while keeping transmitted and logical qubit counts. The authors derive a bound on the resulting distance loss and give conditions for preserving the original distance. In an analysis of random codes with five to eight transmitted qubits, 14.75% had greater distance than their unassisted counterparts, and 81.4% of those admitted a puncturing choice that keeps the original distance.

entry.title: Bivariate bicycle codes over group algebras: quantum codes built from weighted shifts
entry.summary: Bivariate Bicycle Codes over Group Algebras arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies bivariate bicycle group-algebra (BBGA) quantum error-correcting codes built from weighted shift operators over finite group algebras. The authors give sparsity bounds and present computer-verified examples, including a [[144,16,12]] code over a nonabelian group and a [[18,4,3]] code. They show these examples are inequivalent to ordinary abelian realizations.

entry.title: What physics is for: why classical physics is not the limit of quantum mechanics
entry.summary: What is Physics For? Why Classical Physics is not the Limit of Quantum Mechanics arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines the claim that classical physics is the low-action limit of quantum mechanics. It argues that interpretive problems such as the measurement problem, the subject-object divide, and the nature of scientific representation were already present in classical physics. The authors contend quantum mechanics exposes long-unacknowledged philosophical assumptions rather than breaking cleanly from classical physics. The London-Bauer interpretation and QBism are discussed as examples of this broader reconceptualisation.

entry.title: Near-optimal quantum simulation of open-system lattice dynamics, explained
entry.summary: Near-optimal quantum simulation of lattice Lindbladian dynamics arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how to simulate time evolution under geometrically local Lindbladians on a lattice of qudits. The authors present an algorithm that approximates this evolution for time t on N qudits, with diamond-norm error ε, using geometrically local circuits of depth O(t polylog(Nt/ε)). The authors state that this performance is comparable to the HHKL algorithm for lattice Hamiltonian simulation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend HHKL lattice Hamiltonian simulation to geometrically local Lindbladians, reporting local circuits of depth O(t polylog(Nt/ε)) comparable to HHKL.

entry.title: MASH-PLDM: a partially linearized surface hopping method for nonadiabatic dynamics and nonlinear spectroscopy
entry.summary: A partially linearized mapping approach to surface hopping (MASH-PLDM) for nonadiabatic dynamics and nonlinear spectroscopy arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces MASH-PLDM, a partially linearized version of the mapping approach to surface hopping for simulating nonadiabatic dynamics in molecules. It uses two spin vectors, based on the partially linearized density matrix, to describe either electronic population on one adiabatic surface or coherence on the average surface. The method gives improved results over the original MASH for various scattering problems and spin-boson models, especially where coherences matter. It can also compute multi-time correlation functions, which is demonstrated with a proof-of-principle simulation of time-resolved pump-probe spectroscopy.

entry.title: Near-optimal parallel quantum gate learning with low diamond-distance error
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Parallel Unitary Process Tomography in Diamond Distance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how to learn an unknown quantum gate (unitary process tomography), a key step toward working quantum computers. Sequential circuits were already known to achieve optimal query complexity under diamond-distance error, but it was unclear whether parallel circuits could match this. The authors introduce a new explicit parallel procedure and prove that near-optimal query complexity is achievable with parallel circuits. The gap between parallel and sequential approaches is thus closed up to a logarithmic factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an explicit parallel procedure that reaches near-optimal query complexity in diamond distance, narrowing the gap to sequential circuits to a logarithmic factor.

entry.title: Measuring non-Markovianity via witnesses, avoiding full Choi state reconstruction
entry.summary: Witness-based quantification of non-Markovianity without complete Choi state reconstruction arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes a witness-based framework for quantifying non-Markovianity in open quantum systems that avoids fully reconstructing the Choi state of the intermediate dynamical map. It shows that every witness gives a certifiable lower bound on a geometric resource measure, and that positive-semidefinite witnesses also bound the RHP measure. For amplitude-damping and Pauli dynamics, the optimal positive witnesses reduce to Bell-parity projectors whose values come from a few experimentally accessible correlation measurements.

entry.title: Checking whether projected and full-space open-shell ADAPT-VQE states match
entry.summary: From Projected Subspaces to Full-Space Implementations: Representation-Equivalence Audits for Open-Shell ADAPT-VQE arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper examines whether a state optimized in a symmetry-projected space equals the state from exponentiating the unprojected parent generators. It proposes the target-space invariance condition QAP=0 as an equivalence audit and applies it to a Cu(II) CAS(15e,9o) Hamiltonian, where most Hartree–Fock-origin excitations violate it. The work presents a validation framework rather than a new spin-adapted ADAPT algorithm.

entry.title: Quantum parameter estimation under decoherence in neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: Quantum Estimation under Decoherence in Neutrino Oscillations: Quantum Resources, Flavor Accessibility, and Multiparameter Incompatibility arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies neutrino oscillations as an interferometric system for open-system dynamics, quantum resources and parameter estimation. It distinguishes two decoherence models, propagation-basis dephasing and effective flavor-mode dephasing, and derives concurrence, entanglement of formation and local quantum uncertainty for the two-flavor mode state. A monochromatic three-flavor benchmark compares the quantum Fisher information matrix with flavor Fisher information, and the results are state-level information-geometric benchmarks rather than event-level sensitivity forecasts.

entry.title: Studying Quantum Chaos Measures Beyond the Standard Lindblad Approach
entry.summary: Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators Beyond Lindblad arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs), which measure quantum chaos and information scrambling. Starting from a microscopic model of a subsystem coupled to a random bath, the authors find that OTOC dynamics includes an extra contribution, arising from correlations between replicas, beyond the standard Lindblad approach. This extended formalism better preserves properties such as long-time freeness and captures scrambling more faithfully. The authors also show it can be used to numerically study OTOCs in large closed systems by replacing part of the system with a dissipative boundary.

entry.title: Independent density and coherence skin effects in adaptive fermion circuits
entry.summary: Independent density and coherence skin effects in adaptive fermion circuits arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies adaptive quantum circuits that use measurements and outcome-conditioned feedback to produce nonreciprocal dynamics without postselection. The authors show that density and coherence skin effects in fermion circuits can be tuned independently. The stationary density tilt depends only on measurement strength and feedback displacement, while bulk coherences follow an effective Hatano-Nelson generator set by the conditioned gates through a relative occupation phase. Tuning this phase drives a point-gap topological transition and reverses coherence localization.

entry.title: Is rapid mixing stable? A study of whether fast relaxation in open quantum systems survives local perturbations
entry.summary: Is rapid mixing stable? arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Many open quantum systems governed by Lindbladians relax to steady states quickly, in polylogarithmic time in system size. The paper questions whether local perturbations leave this fast mixing intact. It gives counterexamples showing rapid mixing is not stable in general, even when the steady state is unchanged, and shows arbitrarily weak local Hamiltonian perturbations can destroy it. It also provides sufficient conditions guaranteeing stable rapid mixing for several classes of systems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show rapid mixing is generally unstable via counterexamples and give several sufficient conditions for stable rapid mixing, including quasifree fermionic, commuting, and local spin systems

entry.title: Entanglement spectrum and magic in higher-dimensional free-fermion systems
entry.summary: Entanglement spectrum and magic in higher-dimensional free fermionic systems arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies fermionic non-local magic in higher-dimensional free-fermion systems using the entanglement spectrum. For translationally invariant Gaussian states in strip geometries, dimensional reduction reduces the problem to independent lower-dimensional momentum sectors, giving a logarithmic violation of the boundary law in two dimensions. The authors show that second Rényi fermionic non-local magic is bounded by entanglement capacity and introduce an entanglement-temperature deformation. Applied to the Kitaev model, the response is exponentially suppressed in the Abelian phase and algebraic in the non-Abelian phase. For quenches, random Gaussian circuits are shown to spread diffusively in two spatial dimensions.

entry.title: Fast Hamiltonian engineering via cut polytope geometry
entry.summary: Fast Hamiltonian engineering from cut polytope geometry arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a unified framework for Hamiltonian engineering, which simulates a target Hamiltonian's quantum dynamics using a native entangling system and restricted controls, across 2-local qubit, qudit, and fermionic systems. The authors recast time-optimal engineering as a k-cut polytope problem, prove it NP-complete, and relax it to an elliptope with Krivine-type rounding to generate pulses for a linear program. On Ising, chiral clock, and fermionic Harper-Hofstadter benchmarks, the method achieves near-optimal run times and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, with an O(√m) approximation ratio. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce time-optimal Hamiltonian engineering to a complex k-cut polytope problem, report NP-completeness, and obtain an O(√m) approximation via elliptope relaxation with Krivine rounding, r

entry.title: Digital quantum algorithms for creating and using spin squeezed states
entry.summary: Digital Quantum Algorithms for Generating and Utilizing Spin Squeezed States arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents algorithms for efficiently generating and using spin squeezed states on digital quantum computers. The authors introduce an adaptive local-circuit protocol that prepares states with squeezing parameter ξ in depth O(log 1/ξ), which they prove is optimal for permutation symmetric states. Classical simulations under realistic noise models predict a metrological gain of 4.2 dB beyond the standard quantum limit using 55 superconducting qubits including ancillae. ★★★★ Notable: An adaptive local circuit prepares spin squeezed states in O(log(1/ξ)) depth, an exponential improvement over non-adaptive methods; the authors report a matching entanglement lower bound and noisy sim

entry.title: Out-of-time-order correlators in tunable Volcano potentials
entry.summary: Out-of-time-order Correlators in Volcano potentials arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs), a diagnostic of quantum scrambling and chaos, for Volcano potentials. This family interpolates between bounded wells and confining walls and includes the Pöschl-Teller potential. Using numerical diagonalization and semiclassical analysis, the authors examine parameter regimes with both positive and negative curvature. They find that short-time exponential OTOC growth does not necessarily indicate global quantum chaos, but correlates with excited states sampling negative-curvature regions.

entry.title: Asymptotically Optimal Mixed-State Cloning (theory of copying quantum mixed states at scale)
entry.summary: Asymptotically Optimal Mixed-State Cloning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper determines the asymptotic global fidelity of cloning generic mixed states with simple full-rank spectra, with n inputs and m_n outputs such that m_n/n tends to γ>1 in fixed dimension d. It gives an optimal fidelity formula when the spectrum is known and a spectrum-independent cloner when it is unknown, shown to be minimax optimal. For flat projector states, the optimum is also derived, and the proposed cloners are shown to strictly outperform the purify–clone–trace (PCT) method for simple full-rank spectra and rank-r projectors with 1<r<d.

entry.title: Measuring quantum gains in joint current precision in open systems
entry.summary: Characterizing quantum precision enhancement for multiple currents in open quantum systems arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper derives a multi-current kinetic uncertainty relation (MKUR) that bounds the precision of multiple currents in classical nonequilibrium steady states. It compares a quantum system with a classical emulator having the same average currents to identify when quantum coherence reduces joint current fluctuations below the classical limit. The approach is illustrated with a coherently driven two-level system and a three-level heat engine with parasitic environmental couplings.

entry.title: Chern-number estimation: near-optimal quantum algorithm with provable speedup
entry.summary: Chern-number estimation: nearly optimal quantum algorithm and provable quantum speedup arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm for estimating the Chern number, a topological invariant, of a smooth Hamiltonian family over a two-dimensional parameter torus with a unique gapped ground state, including interacting many-body systems. Its Hamiltonian-oracle evolution time is Õ(L_xL_y/Δ_min³), and the authors prove a matching worst-case oracle lower bound, even when the Chern number is promised to be zero or one, so the algorithm is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. They also show that exact Chern-number computation for local Hamiltonian families is in FBQP and BQP-hard. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present a nearly optimal quantum algorithm for Chern-number estimation, with evolution time Õ(L_xL_y/Δ_min³), a matching worst-case oracle lower bound, and BQP-completeness results for top

entry.title: Topological band theory for quantum Hall systems with high-dimensional flux parameter spaces.
entry.summary: Topological Band Theory for High-Dimensional Parameter Spaces arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies topological band theory for quantum Hall systems whose adiabatic flux parameters form a high-dimensional manifold. Such settings arise for strongly correlated matter on Riemann surfaces of genus greater than one and for matter on compact oriented manifolds coupled to p-form gauge potentials. The topological invariants on the parameter space include higher-order curvature terms beyond the first Chern class, which contribute topologically protected terms to Kubo-like formulae. The authors illustrate these ideas with a hyperbolic band theory example based on the genus-two Bolza Riemann surface, a case recently simulated on a synthetic-dimension platform.

entry.title: Proving that deciding whether the multiparameter quantum Fisher information is attainable is NP-hard
entry.summary: Deciding the Attainability of the Multiparameter Quantum Fisher Information is NP-Hard arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The quantum Fisher information sets a bound on the precision of estimating several parameters at once, but a general condition for reaching this bound with measurements on single copies of a state has been missing. This paper proves that deciding exact attainability is NP-hard, even for a restricted class of real, constant-rank quantum models. The proof reduces from deciding whether a bipartite density matrix is separable. Unless P=NP, no efficiently computable necessary and sufficient criterion exists in general. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report reducing multiparameter QFI attainability to separability and proving it NP-hard, presented as a resolution of a long-open question and a fundamental computational obstruction.

entry.title: Constant-depth circuits that prepare 1D quantum Gibbs states
entry.summary: One-dimensional quantum Gibbs states in constant circuit depth arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proves that the Gibbs state of any spin chain at any constant temperature is exactly a mixture of product states over bounded-length blocks of qubits. This implies such states can be prepared by constant-depth local unitary circuits with efficient classical preprocessing. The authors also obtain analogous results for 1D local fermionic Hamiltonians. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report an exact decomposition of any 1D spin-chain Gibbs state into bounded-block product mixtures, giving constant-depth preparation and constant bounds on entanglement depth, width, and

entry.title: Detecting Low-Frequency Gravitational Waves via Gravito-Magnetism
entry.summary: Low Frequency Gravitational Wave Detection with Gravito-Magnetism arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes a method to detect low-frequency gravitational waves (10 nHz to 1 µHz) that separates the signal from asteroid-belt gravity gradient noise. It exploits the gravito-magnetic component of gravitational waves, measured through the Lorentz-type acceleration of test masses. The authors argue this is metrologically feasible and show it allows unambiguous signal extraction in a three-satellite constellation. Atom interferometers are proposed as the isolated inertial reference.

entry.title: Sampling gauge field plaquettes exactly for lattice gauge theories via local constraint solves
entry.summary: Multilevel Plaquette-Space Sampling for Lattice Gauge Theories with Local Constraint Solves arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes a multilevel normalizing-flow method that samples lattice gauge theory configurations directly in plaquette space while enforcing Bianchi constraints exactly. A coarse-to-fine factorization turns a globally coupled constraint problem into a sequence of local solves. The method is validated for U(1) in two and four dimensions and for SU(2) in two dimensions, where it outperforms link-space baselines, with the advantage growing toward weak coupling.

entry.title: A silicon-on-SiC chip platform for coupling to telecom-band vanadium defects
entry.summary: A Si-on-SiC Platform for Interfacing with Vanadium Dopants in the Telecom O-Band arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper presents a silicon-on-SiC photonic platform in which silicon nanocavities evanescently couple to shallow vanadium dopants in commercial 4H-SiC, improving photon collection at the zero-phonon line. The authors report high-purity single-photon emission from isolated vanadium centers with a Purcell-enhanced lifetime of 109 ns. The full optical interface runs through a single lensed fiber, including a 905 nm repump laser. The work positions the platform as a scalable route to telecom-wavelength spin-photon interfaces.

entry.title: Speed-Fisher Information: A Unified Measure of Chaos and Irreversibility
entry.summary: Speed-Fisher Information: Chaos and Irreversibility in Classical and Quantum Dynamics arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proposes a unified way to study classical and quantum chaos by measuring how a system's stationary states respond to slow driving. This sensitivity to average protocol speed is called speed-Fisher information and is linked to irreversible entropy production. The authors show that chaos appears as divergence of this information with protocol time, controlled by low-frequency spectral weight of the perturbation. The approach applies to Hamiltonian quantum and classical systems and extends to non-Hamiltonian classical flows, illustrated with simple examples.

entry.title: An Optimal Quantum Linear Systems Algorithm: Tight Query Bounds for Solving Linear Equations on Quantum Computers
entry.summary: An Optimal Quantum Linear Systems Algorithm arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies the quantum linear systems problem, where one has query access to a sparse matrix A with condition number κ and must produce a quantum state approximating the solution x of Ax = b. The authors show the query complexity is Θ(κ√d·log(1/ε)), improving previous upper and lower bounds. They also resolve an open question of Berry and Childs by showing any N×N unitary can be implemented with bounded error using O(√N) matrix-entry queries. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a tight Θ(κ√d log(1/ε)) query bound for quantum linear systems, improving prior bounds and resolving an open problem of Berry and Childs.

entry.title: The Power of Oracle Access: Optimal Complexity for the Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem
entry.summary: The power of oracle access: Optimal sample and query complexity of the abelian state hidden subgroup problem arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the state hidden subgroup problem, which asks for the symmetries of an unknown quantum state. For finite abelian groups, it gives a query-model algorithm using O(log(|G/H|)/√ε) forward and inverse queries together with a matching lower bound. In the sample model it shows Θ(log(|G/H|)/ε) copies are necessary and sufficient. The quadratic improvement in ε therefore comes from coherent access to the preparation circuit. ★★★★★ Notable: The paper studies the abelian state hidden subgroup problem, giving an O(log|G/H|/√ε) query algorithm with a matching lower bound and Θ(log|G/H|/ε) sample complexity, with applications to stabilizer g

entry.title: Optimal performance of a chaotic Floquet quantum battery, explained as a quantum device that stores and releases energy.
entry.summary: Optimal performance in a chaotic Floquet quantum battery arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies a battery of N uniformly interacting qubits charged by periodic transverse kicks and disorder in the interaction direction. Disorder takes the dynamics out of the permutation-symmetric subspace, increasing stored energy; in the large-disorder limit, random matrix theory gives exact results and energy fluctuations become negligible. With dephasing noise in the storage phase, large disorder keeps ergotropy close to stored energy, with efficiency approaching unity.

entry.title: Electrothermal behavior of superconducting nanowires in a commercial CMOS process
entry.summary: Electrothermal behavior of superconducting nanowires buried in a commercial CMOS process arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies titanium nitride nanowires built in the polysilicon resistor layer of a 22 nm FD-SOI commercial CMOS process. The authors measure current-voltage characteristics and compare retrapping currents with thermal models of longitudinal conduction and interfacial phonon cooling. They find interfacial cooling dominates and report an effective cooling coefficient and film thermal conductivity.

entry.title: Exponential lower bounds for low-degree strategies in quantum position-based cryptography
entry.summary: Exponential lower bounds for low-degree strategies in position-based quantum cryptography arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies lower bounds on the resources needed for non-local quantum computation (NLQC), in which two distant players cooperatively implement a bipartite unitary. The authors consider a family of diagonal ±1 unitaries indexed by Boolean hypercube elements and show that, under a low-degree polynomial condition on the first round, implementing at least one of them requires resources growing exponentially. The result matters for the security of position-based quantum cryptography, and the proof relies on type constants of particular Banach spaces and random estimates of Boolean functions. ★★★★ Notable: Addressing the open problem of exponential NLQC lower bounds, the authors report resource scaling of exp(Ω(n^{2δ}/(log n)^2)) for low-degree strategies, proved via Banach space type constants.

entry.title: Asymmetric Errors in Noisy Quantum Computer Experiments
entry.summary: Analysis of asymmetric errors in NISQ experiments arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper extends earlier analyses of NISQ experiments, including Google's 2019 quantum supremacy experiment, with a focus on asymmetric readout errors. The authors use experimental data and simulations to examine how gate and readout errors affect the fractions of zeros and ones in the output samples. For 12 to 53 qubits, Google's experimental data show that these fractions reflect only the reported asymmetry in readout errors, with no sign of the increased zero fraction predicted for amplitude damping gate errors.

entry.title: Where coherence comes from in quantum and classical induced-coherence interferometers, and how to control it
entry.summary: Induced Coherence in Quantum and Classical Interferometry: Origin and Control arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies wave-particle duality in induced-coherence interferometers, a type of interference setup. Earlier work showed that Young's double-slit interference obeys a triality relation linking coherence, predictability, and entanglement. The authors show this triality persists in the quantum induced-coherence interferometer, while the classical version reduces to the well-known duality inequality. They also examine the origin and control of coherence and entanglement, finding that path indistinguishability plays a complementary role in both.

entry.title: How fast can a parent estimate its children's value? A quantum algorithm for stochastic games
entry.summary: How fast can a parent estimate the value of their children? A quantum algorithm for stochastic games arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm for two-player stochastic games whose trees alternate adversarial and chance layers. It estimates the game's value using queries to leaf values and gives an upper bound on the query complexity. The authors show that quadratic speedups known for adversarial trees and single expectations both carry over when nested. ★★★★ Notable: Gives a depth-exponential bound nesting quantum adversarial search with mean estimation; the authors report both quadratic speedups survive the composition.

entry.title: Electron decoherence from cylindrical holes and circular apertures in metal films
entry.summary: Electron decoherence in cylindrical holes and circular apertures arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how fast free electrons lose coherence when passing through two canonical geometries: a cylindrical hole in a realistic metal and a circular aperture in a thin perfectly conducting film. Using an electromagnetic Green-tensor approach with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and full retardation, the authors derive decoherence probability and elastic phase. For the cylindrical hole, a universal expression linear in temperature emerges in the high-conductivity, high-temperature limit.

entry.title: Circuit design rules for placing gates and entanglement in quantum neural networks using Fourier analysis
entry.summary: Fourier-Geometric Circuit Design for Gate and Entanglement Placement in Quantum Neural Networks arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper gives an explicit rule for arranging local rotations and entangling layers in a parameterized quantum circuit so that a target Fourier coefficient of its output can contribute. It decomposes operator space into frequency-indexed two-dimensional invariant planes using the adjoint action of the encoding generator. The design is validated on a single encoding layer through a placement ablation, regression tasks from PDEBench and physics-informed Maxwell field modeling, and tests showing robustness to moderate simulated gate noise and damping.

entry.title: Trade-offs in high-dimensional time-bin entanglement for quantum key distribution
entry.summary: Temporal trade-offs in high-dimensional entanglement: a comprehensive noise model for optimal time-bin QKD protocols arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines whether high-dimensional time-bin entanglement or simpler qubit encodings give better results in quantum key distribution. The authors study single Franson-based interferometers, using asymptotic key rate and shared entanglement as main metrics, and introduce a flexible noise model covering the relevant parameters. They find that high-dimensional encoding can still outperform qubit-based protocols in some regions when the pair arrival rate is limited, for example by loss or limited pump power.

entry.title: Making HEOM simulations of strongly coupled open quantum systems more numerically stable
entry.summary: Improving the Stability of the Hierarchical Equations of Motion for Open Quantum Systems with Strong Coupling to Structured Bosonic Baths arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) method simulates open quantum systems, but truncating its hierarchy for bosonic baths can cause numerical instability. The authors use an auxiliary Fock-space picture to identify unbalanced hierarchy-raising terms and apply a non-unitary similarity transformation that balances them, reducing their numerical impact. They demonstrate the approach on a spin-boson model with a Brownian oscillator spectral density and then a structured spectral density, reporting that it permits simulations at much stronger system-bath coupling.

entry.title: A classical algorithm that efficiently estimates coarse-grained Boson Sampling statistics.
entry.summary: Efficient classical algorithm for estimating linear statistics of Boson Sampling arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies a type of coarse-grained statistic for Boson Sampling, called linear statistics, which are linear functions of output photon occupation numbers. The authors present an efficient classical algorithm that approximates these statistics within additive error for input states such as Fock and squeezed states. The framework unifies prior results on simulating molecular vibronic spectra and classically approximating detector-binned distributions. The algorithm can also classically evaluate a proposed Boson Sampling-based one-way function, while other cryptographic proposals fall outside its scope.

entry.title: Fixed-time Gaussian state transfer using only collective dissipation
entry.summary: Fixed-Time Gaussian State Transfer via Collective Dissipation in a Fully Static Architecture arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes a fully static method for transferring Gaussian quantum states using only dissipation from collective coupling to a shared environment, with no coherent transport or time-dependent control. An analytic transfer time is derived. Amplitude-level asymmetries leave performance largely unaffected, while phase-level detuning disrupts transfer and produces revival behavior. In the fast-memory regime, the channel recovers the Markovian limit.

entry.title: A dilation theorem for continuous quantum stochastic processes
entry.summary: Dilation theorem for continuum quantum stochastic processes arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a dilation theorem for continuum quantum stochastic processes, linking stochastic dynamics on a system to deterministic Schrödinger evolution on a larger space. The authors show that any continuous process tensor can be approximated arbitrarily well by an explicit closed description in which system and environment are coupled by a bounded Hamiltonian. These regular representations form a dense, easily handled subspace, enabling a continuum version of Choi duality and a rigorous treatment of continuum controls.

entry.title: Heuristic lower bounds on real Grothendieck constants, finite and infinite
entry.summary: Heuristic lower bounds on real Grothendieck constants of finite and infinite order arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes candidate lower bounds on the real Grothendieck constants K_G(d) and their infinite-dimensional limit K_G using rotationally invariant cubic kernels. It identifies a threshold above which hemispherical binary strategies become unstable under cubic boundary deformations, and conjectures these strategies are globally optimal there. If true, this gives K_G ≥ 9π/16, improving the rigorous bound 6π/11. Large-scale optimization supports these predictions and suggests improved bounds for dimensions 4 to 24.

entry.title: Circuit-level benchmarks of GKP-concatenated qLDPC codes: comparing finite-rate outer codes under realistic noise
entry.summary: Circuit-level benchmarks of GKP-concatenated qLDPC Codes arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper benchmarks BB and tricycle quantum LDPC codes as outer codes for GKP concatenation using a unified simulation framework, from code-capacity noise to repeated noisy syndrome extraction with schedule-resolved displacement propagation. In the full circuit model, analog-informed BP-OSD decoding gives thresholds of about 0.212 for the selected BB sequence and 0.142 for the tricycle sequence, corresponding to squeezing requirements of roughly 10.46 dB and 13.94 dB. The results indicate analog GKP information still improves decoding under circuit noise, and the selected BB sequence shows a higher finite-size crossing estimate.

entry.title: Generalized LIMDDs: Compact, Canonical Decision Diagrams Modulo a Group
entry.summary: Generalized LIMDDs: Succinctness and Canonicity for Decision Diagrams Modulo a Group arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper studies decision diagrams for functions from {0,1}^n to C, where residual nodes are merged when they lie in one orbit of a group and the group element is recorded on edges. The group family is generated by phase rotations of order q with up to k control qubits, with or without bit flip X. The authors show exponential succinctness gains over Pauli-LIMDD, and give a five-rule reduction system with unique normal forms computable in polynomial time. ★★★★ Notable: Generalizes Myhill-Nerode quotients to group actions, reporting exponential succinctness gains over Pauli-LIMDD and a unique normal form computable in polynomial time.

entry.title: Gauge freedom and efficient algorithms for learning open quantum system dynamics
entry.summary: Gauge freedom and efficient algorithms for Lindbladian learning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies learning a local Lindbladian, which describes open quantum system dynamics, in the presence of state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) noise. SPAM noise can make distinct Lindbladians experimentally indistinguishable, so part of the Lindbladian is unlearnable. The authors characterize this obstruction and present SPAM-robust algorithms that learn every universally gauge-invariant component using only trusted single-qubit operations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show SPAM noise can make distinct Lindbladians indistinguishable, characterize gauge freedom, and give SPAM-robust learning algorithms using Õ(ε⁻²log(N/δ)) experiments and evolution time.

entry.title: An exact polynomial bridge from task to prediction risk for time-multiplexed photonic quantum reservoirs
entry.summary: An Exact Polynomial Task-Risk Bridge for Time-Multiplexed Photonic Quantum Reservoirs arXiv · Sep 28, 2026Time-multiplexed photonic reservoirs are usually judged by scores on a few datasets and designed by simulating candidate circuits one at a time. For time-unrolled passive linear networks with data-modulated gates or sources and a ridge readout, the authors derive an exact link from the task to the prediction risk in three steps: task features, encoding, and readout. They report that all exact statements agree with numerical checks on seven datasets to machine precision, so candidate architectures can be pruned without trial simulation.

entry.title: A civilization technology scale combining the Kardashev and Barrow scales
entry.summary: A technological capability scale for civilizations from the Kardashev and Barrow scales arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes a technological capability scale that ranks civilizations by the number of control operations they can perform per second, where a control operation sets one binary degree of freedom of matter to a specified value. Drawing on constructor theory, it groups tasks into construction and its special cases on information media: processing, storage and transfer. The index Ξ = K + B adds the Kardashev index K to an efficiency index B based on energy per operation. The authors place humanity at K = 0.73 and B = -0.78, and describe an ultimate technology at Ξ = 7.58.

entry.title: Exact distributions of complex spacing ratios in non-Hermitian random matrices
entry.summary: Exact probability distributions of complex spacing ratios in non-Hermitian random matrices arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies the complex spacing ratio, the ratio of complex displacements from a reference eigenvalue to its nearest and next-to-nearest neighbors, which diagnoses spectral correlations and nonintegrability in open quantum systems. Starting from exact joint eigenvalue densities, the authors derive finite-N distributions for Gaussian non-Hermitian random matrix ensembles in classes AI† and AII†. For AII† they give an exact algebraic expression for arbitrary N and evaluate distributions for N=3 to 6. For AI† they derive a normalized one-dimensional integral representation at N=3, analyze its asymptotics, and confirm the results by numerical diagonalization.

entry.title: Generating vector-vortex gamma photons via nonlinear Compton scattering
entry.summary: Generating Vector-Vortex γ Photons by Nonlinear Compton Scattering arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes a new method to generate vector-vortex gamma photons, whose polarization and orbital angular momentum are nonseparably coupled, using nonlinear Compton scattering in elliptically polarized laser pulses. The authors report that tuning laser ellipticity directs multiphoton absorption to coherently populate orbital angular momentum modes with winding numbers ±ℓ, producing spin-OAM nonseparable photon states. For moderate-intensity linearly polarized lasers, they state the mode-pair concurrence reaches unity for MeV gamma photons.

entry.title: Numerical Study of Laser Slowing, Cooling and Trapping of Positronium
entry.summary: Positronium Laser Deceleration, Cooling and Trapping arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper numerically studies laser deceleration, cooling and trapping of fast ortho-positronium bunches produced in silica microchannel targets from positron bunches of a Surko trap. The authors report that standard Doppler cooling on the 1³S–2³P transition can simultaneously slow, cool and optically trap the atoms. Adding transverse lasers on the 2³P–3³D transition and including full Zeeman manifolds improves timing and final temperature. The required millijoule, roughly 100 ns laser pulses are said to be within current technology.

entry.title: Running large IQP quantum circuit Born machines on smaller quantum hardware by injecting noise
entry.summary: Deployment of Large IQP Circuit Born Machines on Qubit-Limited Hardware Using Noise Injection arXiv · Sep 28, 2026Quantum circuit Born machines built from IQP circuits can be trained classically but need quantum computers for sampling, which limits them to hardware with enough qubits. The paper proposes a deployment protocol that injects noise at the logical level to split a large circuit into smaller clusters that fit on qubit-limited processors, with lightweight resampling of known noisy qubits to reduce the resulting error. Simulations and IBM Heron experiments deploying a 316-qubit circuit onto 156-qubit hardware show the mitigation brings the sampled distribution closer to the target. The method also preserves correlation structure more accurately than a classical baseline with accurate single-qubit marginals.

entry.title: Weakly interacting fermion Gibbs states are Gaussian mixtures and classically simulable
entry.summary: Weakly interacting fermionic Gibbs states are Gaussian mixtures and classically simulable arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper proves that for sufficiently weak interactions, the Gibbs state of a local fermionic Hamiltonian at any finite temperature and in any spatial dimension is a convex mixture of fermionic Gaussian states. Building on this structure, the authors construct a polynomial-time classical sampler that generates samples from the Gibbs state using Metropolis updates on a tree whose leaves are Gaussian states. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that for weak enough interactions, Gibbs states of local fermionic Hamiltonians are convex mixtures of Gaussian states, and build a polynomial-time classical sampler via Metropolis

entry.title: Overlap Gap Property: Showing Where Quantum Optimization Beats Quantum-Inspired Classical Methods
entry.summary: The Overlap Gap Property: Separating Quantum and Quantum-Inspired Approximate Optimization Algorithms arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper proves that the Mean-Field Approximate Optimization Algorithm, a classical quantum-inspired version of QAOA, cannot find arbitrarily near-optimal solutions for problems with the Overlap Gap Property. It links this limitation to finite-memory Approximate Message Passing algorithms. Numerical simulations on Max-4-XORSAT instances with this property show that QAOA can get past the barrier.

entry.title: Quantum codes with addressable transversal T gates that stay efficient at scale
entry.summary: Asymptotically Good Quantum Codes with Addressable Transversal T Gates arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper constructs a family of binary CSS quantum codes with constant rate and linear distance. These codes support fully addressable transversal T gates, so any chosen tensor product of logical T powers is realized by physical T powers without later correction. The construction combines algebraic-geometry codes with a binary embedding, and the minimum embedding length is formulated as a minimum-weight problem, which improves the constants in the asymptotic bounds numerically.

entry.title: A method for approximating quantum correlation functions with accuracy and a rigorous error bound
entry.summary: Accurate and bounded approximation of quantum correlation functions arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper addresses the classical simulation of non-integrable quantum many-body dynamics, which becomes intractable for larger systems. For the infinite-temperature correlation function, it derives a rigorous error bound for approximating the full dynamics within a computable finite-sized region. Applied to autocorrelations, the finite-region approach is shown to be especially accurate across one-dimensional systems and beyond. It can also provide rigorous error bounds for other approximate methods, demonstrated on matrix-product-operator simulations.

entry.title: Deriving the classical LLG equation from quantum spin dynamics
entry.summary: From Quantum to Classical Dissipative Spin Dynamics arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation describes dissipative magnetization dynamics. This paper shows that the LLG equation arises as the classical large-spin limit of the quantum LLG (QLLG) equation. The result is verified analytically and numerically for an interacting spin system. The authors also find that quantum effects become less noticeable as the number of spins in the Hamiltonian increases.

entry.title: Quantum state transfer for polynomial states via relative decoding
entry.summary: From Simple Sources to Quantum Advantage: Homomorphic Polynomial Transduction via Relative Decoding arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper recasts decoded quantum interferometry (DQI) and its Hamiltonian extension (HDQI) as quantum state transduction through algebra homomorphisms, moving polynomial operator states from a source Hamiltonian to a target Hamiltonian. It proves that a relative distance greater than 2D is equivalent to preserving all inner products between degree-D polynomials. For a nonlinear pairwise optimization variant, the authors report an ideal quantum score of 0.643 versus 0.606 for the best tested classical heuristic.

entry.title: Classical limit on information rate for a dephasing-enhanced quantum neuron
entry.summary: Classical Bound on the Fisher Information Rate of a Dephasing-Enhanced Quantum Neuron arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies a single-qubit dissipative quantum neuron updated by partial resets at rate ν and read out by repeated projective measurements. The authors derive an exact local Fisher information rate and show it is bounded by ν(1-s)(1+s)²/2 ≤ 16ν/27 near activation threshold. Optimized over readout interval and retained amplitude, the ideal bound cannot be exceeded by quantum coherence and is saturated by a classical two-state jump process.

entry.title: Experimental demonstration of Grover-based quantum-enhanced sensing
entry.summary: Experimental quantum-computing-enhanced sensing using Grover's algorithm arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper experimentally tests a theoretical proposal that repurposes Grover's search algorithm to better detect signals of unknown frequency across a wide detection bandwidth. The experiments used a single superconducting qubit coupled to a single superconducting cavity. Above a detection bandwidth of 10 MHz, the Grover-based protocol outperformed the non-Grover baseline, with the advantage growing superlinearly. For larger bandwidths and higher accuracy targets, it reduced the required signal by more than 10 times.

entry.title: Enantiomer-specific pumping of chiral molecules in higher rotational states
entry.summary: Enantiomer-specific pumping of chiral molecules in high-J rotational states arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes a scheme for enantiomer-specific state transfer of chiral molecules involving rotational states J=1 and J=2. It uses three linearly polarized microwave fields and one laser beam to pump one enantiomer into an enantiomer-specific dark state, while the other is dissipatively pumped out. The authors state the strategy can be extended to rotational states with higher angular momenta.

entry.title: All-or-nothing demonstration of preparation contextuality
entry.summary: All-vs-Nothing Operational Manifestation of Preparation Contextuality arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper introduces a parity-oblivious Hidden Matching task that demonstrates preparation contextuality in an all-or-nothing way. A quantum protocol using a single ⌈log₂n⌉-qubit message succeeds with certainty. The authors prove that no preparation-noncontextual model can achieve perfect success for any even n≥6. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces a parity-oblivious hidden matching task giving an all-vs-nothing manifestation of preparation contextuality; the authors report that quantum protocols succeed perfectly while noncontextual

entry.title: Fast classical simulation of noisy quantum memory by predicting error-free branches
entry.summary: Classical simulation of amplitude-damped bucket-brigade quantum random access memories via predictable branch evolution arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies how to classically simulate bucket-brigade quantum random access memory (QRAM) under noise. Noise histories are sampled, and branches whose routing paths avoid every sampled fault have predictable final states, so they can be pruned rather than evolved. The authors give a complete analysis for amplitude damping with qutrit and qubit encodings, and revise the pruning criterion for qubit encoding. The algorithm evolves only bad branches plus one reference branch, reaching speedups up to 285 times.

entry.title: Directional pumping of a two-level system by a quantum source with fluctuation regulation
entry.summary: Directional pumping of a two-level system by a fluctuation-regulated quantum source arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper addresses why a resonant classical field only saturates a two-level system and cannot transfer population directionally. By keeping the excitation source as a quantum subsystem and tracing it out, the authors show that its second moments produce upward and downward dissipative channels. For a fully excited, number-diagonal source only the upward channel remains, giving monotonic pumping. With exponentially decaying source correlations, the pumping rate has a Lorentzian detuning dependence, and with thermal relaxation the steady-state excited population can exceed one half.

entry.title: A general measure of correlation for quantum and classical statistical systems
entry.summary: Correlation measure for statistical systems arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes a general measure of correlations for statistical systems called the correlation index. It applies to quantum and classical systems, in both equilibrium and nonequilibrium states. The authors define the index for arbitrary trace-class operators and illustrate it with examples of density operators and reduced density matrices. Equilibrium examples cover bosonic systems including Bose-Einstein condensates, superconducting systems, and spin systems. Nonequilibrium cases are considered for nonlinear dynamics of spin and pseudospin systems.

entry.title: General Photon Subtraction from a Gaussian Perspective: a formalism describing photon-subtracted Gaussian states to improve cat, cubic phase, and GKP state generation.
entry.summary: General Photon Subtraction from a Gaussian Perspective arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper introduces a formalism that applies a Gaussian blur and filter to the measured Fock Wigner function to describe general photon-subtracted Gaussian states. In this picture, initial squeezing, Gaussian measurements, and photon loss all contribute to the total blurring. The authors use it to trade off success rates, feed-forward compatibility, and loss tolerance when improving cat, cubic phase, and GKP state generation. They also introduce the expected Wigner logarithmic negativity as an additive monotone of non-Gaussianity and establish a general lower bound on resources for near-deterministic generation of target states.

entry.title: Simulating Hybrid Qubit-Oscillator Quantum Circuits Using Gaussian Decompositions
entry.summary: Efficient Simulation of Hybrid Continuous- and Discrete-Variable Quantum Circuits via Gaussian Decompositions arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper presents a simulation framework for hybrid quantum systems combining discrete-variable and continuous-variable subsystems, based on linear combinations of Gaussian functions. The hybrid density matrix is split into blocks in a discrete basis, each represented as such an expansion, and analytic formulas are derived for Gaussian operations and controlled Gaussian channels with state-dependent noise. The approach avoids Fock-space truncation of the continuous-variable part. As an example, the authors simulate Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill state generation in a cavity-QED system.

entry.title: Cubic Phase Gate Using a Trapped Ion Oscillator
entry.summary: Cubic Phase Gate with a Trapped Ion Oscillator arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates a method to approximate the cubic phase gate, a nonlinear operation needed for universal continuous-variable quantum computation, using the motion of trapped ions. The authors numerically optimize the phases and amplitudes of state-dependent force pulses and verify performance for vacuum and low-amplitude coherent state inputs. The protocol is also said to extend to approximating other nonlinear unitaries.

entry.title: Log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information: A New Measure of Quantum Conditional Independence
entry.summary: Log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper introduces a quantum Rényi conditional mutual information that measures conditional independence between quantum systems. It is monotone under local quantum channels, additive under tensor products, and monotone in the Rényi parameter, converging to the quantum conditional mutual information as the parameter approaches 1. The authors derive bounds in terms of relative entropies to the Petz-recovered state, leading to improved upper and lower bounds on the QCMI and Rényi chain rules. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a quantum Rényi conditional mutual information that they report has monotonicity and additivity, and derive recovery-based upper and lower bounds on QCMI along with Rényi chain rul

entry.title: Thresholds and chaos in open-system digital quantum simulation
entry.summary: Trotterisation Thresholds and Dissipative Quantum Chaos in Open-System Digital Quantum Simulation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies the Trotter step-size threshold in digital quantum simulation for open systems that include environmental noise and decoherence. It finds that beyond the threshold, simulation accuracy breaks down suddenly, and that this persists even in the steady-state limit. The authors use random matrix theory to characterise the onset of unitary and dissipative quantum chaos, and report that dissipative chaos emerges only when dissipation is strong enough but does not suppress the underlying chaotic structure.

entry.title: Quantum entanglement in quantum classifiers for breast cancer diagnosis
entry.summary: Quantum Entanglement in Variational Quantum Classification for Breast Cancer Diagnosis arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This study compares three three-qubit variational quantum classifiers that differ only in how their qubits are entangled, testing each on the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer dataset. The configuration with the highest entanglement gave slightly higher accuracy and F1-score and was the most stable across folds. The authors found the link between entanglement and performance weak and not significant, so it is an association rather than a proven cause.

entry.title: Microsecond-programmable synthetic quantum matter for Heisenberg-limited metrology without adiabatic evolution
entry.summary: Microsecond-Programmable Synthetic Quantum Matter: Circumventing the Adiabatic Bottleneck for Heisenberg-Limited Metrology arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes a non-adiabatic Floquet protocol in a single-cavity Bose-Einstein condensate that uses rapid rotations and phase jumps to synthesize effective Two-Axis Twisting interactions from native longitudinal couplings. The authors simulate the dynamics with an exact matrix product operator encoding and DMRG/TDVP methods for N=10^3 ensembles, including decoherence. They report rapid generation of Heisenberg-limited spin squeezing, with a phenomenological optimal extraction time near 3.26 microseconds.

entry.title: Energy gap of a confined chiral mode as a measure of critical zero-point fluctuations
entry.summary: Excitation Gap of a Confined Chiral Mode Measures Critical Zero-Point Fluctuations arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies the excitation gap where uniform and chiral superradiant boundaries meet in a quantum Rabi ring. The gap is proportional to the uniform zero-point variance divided by the frequency ratio η, closing as η^-2/3 while the variance grows as η^1/3. A quartic Schrödinger equation matches full spin-photon diagonalization, and a triangle of spins with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange follows the same relation with a different coefficient.

entry.title: Discontinuity of Continuum Fermion Dynamics: how fermion time evolution can break continuity.
entry.summary: Discontinuity of Continuum Fermion Dynamics arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper studies the Heisenberg dynamics of continuum fermions in R^d interacting through a pair potential. For a large class of nonconstant pair potentials, under suitable assumptions on the dispersion relation and external potential, the dynamics is shown not to be pointwise-norm continuous even on the gauge-invariant CAR algebra. An automatic-continuity argument then shows that neither the CAR algebra nor its gauge-invariant subalgebra is invariant under the dynamics, with non-invariance at almost all times.

entry.title: Bound states in the continuum in cavity magnonics using Bragg and anti-Bragg mirrors
entry.summary: Cavity magnonics and bound states in the continuum with Bragg and anti-Bragg mirrors arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates bound states in the continuum (BICs) in cavity magnonics. Two periodic arrays of ferrimagnetic spheres act as mirrors in a dual-open-waveguide setup, forming Bragg and anti-Bragg cavities. A dark supermode couples to a probe magnon, producing a polariton splitting. Moving the probe sphere enables position-dependent detection of the cavity field.

entry.title: Topological edge state observed among localized bulk states in an anisotropic quantum Rabi model
entry.summary: Observation of a topological edge state among localized bulk states in the anisotropic quantum Rabi model arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This study uses a trapped-ion quantum simulator to examine the topological edge state and bulk states of the anisotropic quantum Rabi model. Because the non-uniform couplings break translational symmetry, both the edge state and bulk states are localized, so spatial localization alone cannot distinguish them. The edge state shows well-defined chirality and near-complete spin-boson separability, which the bulk states do not. Phase-space tomography further shows its bosonic component is a squeezed vacuum state with squeezing up to 6.45 dB.

entry.title: Reconstructing nuclear scattering phase shifts on a quantum processor with compressed RODEO circuits
entry.summary: Nuclear scattering phase shifts with factorized geometric-time RODEO on a quantum processor arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper reconstructs elastic s-wave neutron-proton phase shifts from trapped energy spectra measured on an IBM quantum processor using a compressed RODEO circuit. It introduces a six-cycle factorized geometric-time RODEO method (FG-R6) and compares it with ten-cycle direct RODEO at equal qubit width and shot budgets. FG-R6 reduces median compiled depth and two-qubit-gate count and lowers finite-shot energy uncertainty. The authors argue that circuit performance should be judged through the scattering reconstruction and its energy range, not spectral RMS errors alone.

entry.title: Optimal quantum algorithms for finding an item in a sorted list
entry.summary: Optimal Quantum Algorithms for Ordered Search arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies ordered search, which finds a target in a sorted list of size n using comparison queries. It presents two new quantum algorithms, each using the optimal (1/π)ln n + o(log n) queries. The first is a zero-error algorithm derived from a continuum relaxation of the problem. The second is an exact algorithm based on an analytic solution of a polynomial program by Farhi, Goldstone, Gutmann, and Sipser.

entry.title: Quantum memory in an effective Λ-type system using dynamic detuning control of a superconducting qubit pair
entry.summary: Quantum memory in an effective Λ-type system using dynamic detuning control of a superconducting qubit pair arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This theoretical paper studies storing quantum light in an effective Λ-type system made of two tunable superconducting qubits coupled to a semi-infinite transmission line and spaced half a wavelength apart. Their frequency detuning couples a superradiant excited state to a subradiant metastable state. By dynamically adjusting this detuning, an incoming quantum field is mapped into the subradiant collective state, stored as a long-lived excitation, and retrieved on demand. The authors propose the system as a minimal, tunable quantum memory for scalable superconducting quantum networks.

entry.title: Nakayama's reduction of quantum topos and Bayesian quantum computing
entry.summary: Nakayama's reduction of quantum topos and Bayesian quantum computing arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper presents Nakayama's method for limiting contexts in Döring-Isham topos quantum theory, unifying this limitation with the definition of probability as a single topology choice. The authors explain how this unification supports a Bayesian view in which probability changes as data is obtained. They describe this change as a local shift in the applicability of a predictive theory and apply it to quantum computing.

entry.title: Tensor-engineered van der Waals NbOCl2 metasurface for generating polarization-entangled photon pairs
entry.summary: Tensor-Engineered Van der Waals NbOCl2 Resonant Metasurface for Polarization-entangled Bell State Generation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper presents a resonant metasurface built from NbOCl2, a van der Waals nonlinear material, that uses its optical anisotropy to control polarization-dependent nonlinear responses. By tuning resonant modes, the nonlinear response along the c axis is enhanced by three orders of magnitude, and the second-order susceptibility tensor is redistributed between orthogonal polarization channels. The approach yields polarization-entangled photon pairs with a measured fidelity of up to 92%.

entry.title: Native CP2K implementation of the machine-learned Skala exchange-correlation functional for molecular and solid-state calculations
entry.summary: Native implementation of the machine-learned Skala exchange-correlation functional in CP2K: Unified one-centre reconstruction for molecular and condensed-phase calculations arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper implements the machine-learned Skala exchange-correlation functional natively in CP2K's GPW and GAPW methods, using a joint one-centre reconstruction of density, gradients, and kinetic-energy density. For crystalline CO2, NH3, and urea, all-electron Skala-D3(BJ) calculations give a mean absolute error of 1.54 kJ/mol against diffusion Monte Carlo. For the 13 DMC-ICE13 phases, the absolute lattice-energy MAE is 1.16 kJ/mol. However, the LC10 benchmark shows systematically underestimated equilibrium lattice constants, indicating structural overbinding.

entry.title: Moving Quantum Annealing Errors into a Cavity
entry.summary: Swapping Quantum Annealing Errors into a Cavity arXiv · Sep 28, 2026Quantum annealing slows down at small energy gaps, and the errors made there go undetected. The authors propose cavity quantum annealing, which couples a high-frequency cavity mode mid-schedule to swap these errors into photons. In the p-spin model, annealing time drops to nearly the square root of the time needed without the cavity. Counting photons also certifies results, with high-photon runs reaching above 99.99% ground-state fidelity much sooner.

entry.title: Why approximating quantum code distance is computationally hard
entry.summary: Hardness of Approximating Quantum Code Distance Beyond √N arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies how hard it is to approximate the minimum distance of a stabilizer quantum code. Earlier reductions only reached an additive gap of order √N, and this work closes that gap to a linear one. It also begins a fine-grained analysis, giving running-time lower bounds tied to SETH and Gap-ETH. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors raise the additive-gap hardness for approximating quantum stabilizer code distance from O(sqrt(N)) to linear, claiming no randomized algorithm achieves additive alpha*N approximation unles

entry.title: Quantum-computer Kohn-Sham DFT using orthonormalized plane-wave orbitals and a dual-basis eigensolver
entry.summary: Quantum-Computing Self-Consistent Kohn-Sham DFT: Plane-Wave-Orthonormalized Orbitals with a Dual-Basis Quantum Eigensolver arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper presents an all-electron, full-potential Kohn-Sham density functional theory method for quantum computers. It uses a quantum-circuit eigensolver to solve self-consistent field problems in a plane-wave-orthonormalized-orbital basis, solving each step in a contracted basis. For an H8 chain, emulated results agree with classical calculations within 0.02 mHa. On IonQ Forte-1 hardware, the measured energy difference matches the noise-free value within one standard deviation.

entry.title: Controlling two-photon interference with structured pump light to tune the shift from constructive to destructive effects
entry.summary: Nonlinear engineering of Hong-Ou-Mandel interference with structured light arXiv · Sep 28, 2026Two photons entering a Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer bunch or anti-bunch depending on their state's symmetry, producing constructive or destructive interference. This paper tailors the pump field in spontaneous parametric down-conversion, using rotating structured pump modes in Hermite-Gaussian and Laguerre-Gaussian bases. The authors report that the pump's parity shapes the transition from constructive to destructive interference, with sensitivity increasing with mode order in the Hermite-Gaussian case. For Laguerre-Gaussian modes, angular resolution improves by an integer factor proportional to orbital angular momentum content, suggesting potential for Hong-Ou-Mandel-enhanced rotation sensing.

entry.title: Dynamically Controlling Photon Statistics in a Raman-Coupled Cavity QED System
entry.summary: Dynamic Sculpting of Photon Statistics in a Raman-Coupled Cavity QED System arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper proposes a scheme that actively switches photon statistics between bunching and antibunching through quantum interference. It uses a Raman-coupled cavity-atom system with parametric amplification, where time-modulating the intermediate-state detuning either deepens photon blockade or enhances bunching. Simultaneously modulating the cavity and intermediate-state detunings produces antibunching unattainable under static conditions, and it recurs periodically at intervals set by the modulation frequency.

entry.title: Study on how embedding design affects quantum physics-informed neural networks
