entry.summary: On Embedding Design in Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies how the embedding that maps coordinates into quantum states affects quantum physics-informed neural networks (QPINNs) that solve PDEs. The authors introduce a unified embedding framework and propose two embeddings, LQNN-TE-QPINN and AdaFreq-QPINN. They evaluate them on one- and two-dimensional Burgers equations against analytical encodings and other architectures. The results indicate that embedding design substantially influences approximation and optimization behavior.

entry.title: A quantum linear-system algorithm optimal for both oracle query counts
entry.summary: Simultaneously Query-Optimal Quantum Linear-System Algorithm arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper asks whether one quantum algorithm for linear systems can meet the known optimal query bounds for both the matrix block-encoding oracle and the right-hand-side state-preparation oracle at once. Given a constant-factor estimate of the solution norm, the authors present an algorithm using O(κ log(1/ε)) matrix queries and O(κ/s) state-preparation queries. They also prove matching lower bounds on a single Hermitian instance, showing the two bounds are jointly optimal. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a quantum linear-system algorithm achieving O(κ log(1/ε)) matrix queries and O(κ/s) state-preparation queries simultaneously, together with a matching same-instance lower bound on a

entry.title: Effective atom-dimer bands of strongly coupled three-body lattice systems, with exact critical mass ratios and a statistics-quasimomentum duality
entry.summary: Effective atom-dimer bands of three-body lattice systems at strong coupling: exact critical mass ratios and a statistics-quasimomentum duality arXiv · Sep 27, 2026This paper studies three particles on a square lattice with infinitely strong contact interactions, across all total quasimomenta and three statistical cases. Using a Feshbach-Schur reduction, the authors derive effective Hamiltonians with a proved first-order error bound and reduce the threshold problem to a quartic polynomial built from square-lattice two-point resistances. They give the atom-dimer band structure over the Brillouin zone and the critical mass ratio, with the exact value pi/(pi-2) at zero quasimomentum. The paper also proves two dualities relating a change of statistics to a quasimomentum shift by pi.

entry.title: Interactions help time crystals resist dephasing but disrupt order under multipolar drives
entry.summary: Interactions Protect Periodically Driven Time Crystals Against Dephasing but Destabilise Multipolar-Driven Order arXiv · Sep 27, 2026The paper studies a disordered periodically kicked Ising model to see how interaction strength and spin coordination (grid versus ring) affect time-crystal order. For a periodic drive, stronger coupling lengthens the coherence time, whereas for random multipolar drives of order one or higher, doubling the coupling shortens it. At equal total interaction strength, a grid keeps coherence longer than a ring.

entry.title: Controlling Defect-Phonon Interactions in Silicon Carbide Membranes via Heterophase Interfaces
entry.summary: Engineering Defect-Phonon Interactions Through Heterophase-Interfaces in Silicon Carbide Membranes arXiv · Sep 27, 2026This paper uses remote epitaxy to create controlled heterophase interfaces (3C/4H) in silicon carbide membranes and studies how they affect defect-phonon interactions. Compared with single-phase 4H-SiC membranes, silicon vacancy (Vsi) defects at the 3C/4H interface show markedly enhanced zero-phonon optical transitions, with a zero-phonon linewidth of 4.71 meV even at room temperature. The authors conclude that heterophase-interface engineering is an effective way to tailor defect-phonon interactions and realize bright room-temperature quantum emitters.

entry.title: How many light particles a molecule can scatter before losing quantum coherence
entry.summary: How many photons can a molecule scatter before its coherence is lost? arXiv · Sep 27, 2026Molecular qubits trapped in optical traps can lose coherence when they scatter photons from the trapping lasers. The rate has two parts: the mean Raman scattering rate of the two qubit states, and a term proportional to the square of the difference in their Rayleigh scattering amplitudes. The paper calculates the decoherence rate in terms of the molecular polarizability components α1 and α2. It finds decoherence is suppressed at wavelengths where both are small, and identifies such wavelengths for CaF molecules.

entry.title: Local many-worlds quantum mechanics: linking Deutsch-Hayden descriptors to local wavefunctions
entry.summary: Local Many Worlds in Spacetime: Deutsch-Hayden Descriptors and Local Wavefunctions arXiv · Sep 27, 2026The paper presents a local many-worlds formulation of quantum mechanics in spacetime, where each event has its own local wavefunction built only from its past light cone, with no global configuration-space wavefunction and no collapse. The same information is expressed in the Heisenberg picture through Deutsch-Hayden descriptors, which are compact but harder to interpret. The authors show that local wavefunctions for any N-qubit system can be constructed directly from these descriptors.

entry.title: Temperature–Hamiltonian ambiguity in strong-coupling quantum equilibrium
entry.summary: Temperature--Hamiltonian Ambiguity in Strong-Coupling Quantum Equilibrium arXiv · Sep 27, 2026In strong coupling, a subsystem's reduced equilibrium state fixes the Gibbs generator but not, by itself, the local Hamiltonian and temperature. The authors propose identifying the local Hamiltonian from physical information independent of the stationary state, after which a compatible exact reduced state determines a unique local temperature. Examples include an exactly solvable two-level-system–oscillator model and an exact bosonic model.

entry.title: Calibrating quantum priors with fidelity structure for single-circuit QGAN image generation
entry.summary: Quantum Fidelity Landscape-Guided Prior Calibration for Single-Circuit QGAN Image Generation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies pixel-level, end-to-end image generation with a single-quantum-circuit Quantum Generative Adversarial Network (QGAN), avoiding patch-based decomposition. The authors introduce the Quantum Fidelity Landscape (QFL) and use it to calibrate the quantum prior before adversarial training, in a framework called BasicQGAN. On small grayscale image datasets, the method achieves stable generation while requiring fewer qubits and trainable parameters than representative patch-based quantum generators.

entry.title: Quantum Computing for Network Security Classification: Near-Term and Long-Term Memory Efficiency
entry.summary: Quantum Computing for Network Security Classification: Near-Term Classification and Long-Term Memory Efficiency arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines how quantum computing may help network-security classification through two experiments. First, quantum-kernel SVMs are compared with classical SVM baselines on KDD Cup 1999, CICIDS2017, and BoT-IoT, finding quantum kernels competitive in some settings while classical RBF kernels remain stronger in others. Second, quantum oracle sketching is used to study memory efficiency for classifying streaming data, showing that comparable accuracy requires a much smaller effective memory size than explicit sparse or QRAM-style storage. The authors suggest the long-term value may lie in memory-efficient data access rather than immediate runtime speedup.

entry.title: Degree balance sets a fine-grained complexity boundary for quantum SAT
entry.summary: Degree Balance as a Fine-Grained Complexity Boundary for Quantum SAT arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the local Hamiltonian problem, a QMA-complete problem, under fine-grained complexity. Assuming the Hamiltonian is frustration-free on YES instances and approximately regular, the authors give classical and quantum algorithms that are exponentially faster than brute force. Assuming (Q)SETH, they show quantum 5-SAT has no non-trivial worst-case speedup, even when only O(√n) qubits have high degree. Reducing that high-degree set or its degrees by a factor of n^δ yields an O(2^{(1-ε)n}) algorithm. ★★★★ Notable: Under frustration-freeness and approximate regularity, the authors give exponential speedups and report a (Q)SETH lower bound nearly matching this boundary, forming a fine-grained dichotomy.

entry.title: From Classical to Quantum Channels: Positive Covert Communication Rates
entry.summary: From Classical to Quantum Channels: Achieving Positive Covert Rates arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines when covert communication at positive rates is possible over discrete memoryless classical, classical-quantum, and quantum channels. For classical point-to-point channels, positive covert rates are achievable for certain channel classes when the input alphabet is larger than the output alphabet. For quantum channels, if the innocent state is mixed, a non-trivial input ensemble can always satisfy the covertness constraint. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give new conditions for positive covert rates over classical, cq, and quantum channels, extending to MACs; they report that input dimension exceeding output dimension yields achievability.

entry.title: Learning sparse quantum states using only single-qubit measurements
entry.summary: Learning sparse quantum states from single-qubit measurements arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies learning sparse quantum states, whose density matrices have at most s nonzero entries in an unknown product basis. It shows such states, even with long-range entanglement, can be learned efficiently using only single-qubit measurements, without entangling gates. For constant sparsity, sample and classical computational complexity are polynomial. For sparsity growing polynomially with n, sample complexity remains polynomial. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show sparse long-range-entangled states can be learned from single-qubit measurements alone, with polynomial sample and classical complexity for constant sparsity, and quasipolynomial clas

entry.title: Evaluating Machine Unlearning in Materials Science: Retraining Baselines and the Deletion Floor
entry.summary: Bounding Retraining Equivalence and the Deletion Floor in Materials Machine Unlearning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper notes that in materials machine learning, closely related retained data can keep property predictions accurate after a record is deleted, so post-deletion error is an ambiguous measure of unlearning. The authors define the deletion floor as the expected target loss under a specified retraining procedure for the deleted request, and provide theoretical bounds and empirical comparisons. They recommend reporting reference loss, prediction change, and retained utility together.

entry.title: Low-weight canonical logical bases built from pair-partition codes
entry.summary: Low-Weight Canonical Logical Bases from Pair-Partition Codes arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper builds complete canonical logical bases for qubit CSS codes by assigning quaternary coefficients to binary circulant permutation matrix pair-partition checks, then constructing, normalizing, and expanding logical representatives into binary matrices. It reports parameters, check ranks, and basis weights for seven binary codes. For example, the [[2048,512,24]] code has canonical logical representatives with binary weight 27 on both the X and Z sides.

entry.title: QC-Stark: A Multi-Task Benchmark Showing Uneven LLM Abilities on Quantum Computing Tasks
entry.summary: QC-Stark: A Multi-Task Benchmark Revealing Capability Dissociations in LLMs Evaluated on Quantum Computing Tasks arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper introduces QC-Stark, a benchmark that tests large language models on 11 quantum computing tasks, including circuit construction, debugging, compilation, error correction, and simulation. In 2,750 evaluations, overall model rankings were found to hide large differences between individual tasks. For 4 of the 11 tasks, the correlation between overall and per-task rankings was statistically insignificant.

entry.title: Quantum query complexity beyond worst-case inputs using smoothed analysis
entry.summary: Quantum Query Complexity Beyond the Worst Case arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper brings smoothed analysis, a classical framework for explaining algorithm performance beyond worst-case inputs, into quantum query complexity. It shows a total function whose smoothed quantum query complexity is exponentially smaller than its classical query complexity. It also gives near-tight characterizations for symmetric Boolean functions and quantum speedups for string problems such as pattern matching and edit distance. ★★★★ Notable: The first systematic study of quantum smoothed analysis; the abstract reports an exponential query complexity separation and near-tight characterizations for symmetric Boolean functions that unify pri

entry.title: Sublinear Pauli-measurement protocol for estimating quantum fidelity
entry.summary: Sublinear Copies Suffice for Fidelity Estimation with Pauli Measurements arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper presents a protocol for estimating the quantum fidelity, to precision ε, between a known target state and an unknown lab-prepared state. The protocol uses a sublinear number of Pauli basis measurements, o(d^0.9908/ε²). The source abstract states only this result and gives no further detail.

entry.title: Distributional variants of a quantum complexity conjecture
entry.summary: Distributional Variants of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies a conjecture asking whether quantum query algorithms under uniform random inputs can be simulated by classical ones with only polynomial overhead. The authors examine analogous conjectures for biased product distributions and for uniform distributions over Hamming-weight slices. They prove these variants are all equivalent to the original uniform-distribution conjecture. They also formulate distributional versions of the stronger Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture and show those are equivalent to the original as well.

entry.title: Computational complexity of Clifford template compilation and whether quantum computers help
entry.summary: Computational Complexity of Clifford Template Compilation: Are Quantum Computers Useful for Compiling Quantum Circuits? arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies how to choose repetition counts for a finite sequence of repeatable Clifford operations so that the resulting template realizes a target transformation of Pauli operators. For commuting templates with unrestricted integer exponents, feasibility is in NP∩BQP and a quantum algorithm can construct a solution. Restricting exponents to {0,1} makes feasibility NP-complete, while for commuting self-inverse cases binary feasibility is classically polynomial-time but bounding the total repetition count is NP-complete.

entry.title: Simulation-based inference of quantum system parameters with neural posterior estimation
entry.summary: Simulation-Based Quantum System Inference with Neural Posterior Estimation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes a likelihood-free framework that learns parameter posteriors for quantum systems directly from classical simulation data, addressing the intractable likelihoods caused by exponentially large Hilbert spaces. It pairs polynomial-cost classical simulators, such as Pauli propagation and tensor networks, with normalizing flows or other neural density estimators, so one trained model maps any new measurement record to its posterior in a single forward pass. The authors numerically demonstrate the approach on Pauli noise learning, quantum error mitigation, state tomography, and Hamiltonian learning, noting that posterior uncertainty also diagnoses non-identifiability.

entry.title: Constant-depth circuits for arbitrary single-qubit gate synthesis, with matching depth bounds
entry.summary: Depth-Optimal Quantum Compilation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper presents the first constant-depth circuit for synthesizing arbitrary single-qubit gates, a construction that is fully unitary and needs no pre-supplied catalyst. With only bounded-width gates, it achieves depth O(log log(1/ε)) and proves a matching lower bound. The authors also show that Hadamard, T, and generalized Toffoli gates suffice for constant-depth synthesis, and derive new structural results about shallow quantum circuit complexity. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first constant-depth circuit for arbitrary single-qubit gate synthesis, report a matching Ω(log log(1/ε)) depth lower bound for bounded-width gates, and show a depth-preserving re

entry.title: Faster quantum algorithms for low-energy states of k-local Hamiltonians, with near-optimal density bounds
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Bounds on the Density of Low-Energy States of k-Local Hamiltonians and Faster Quantum Algorithms arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies low-energy estimation and state preparation for general k-local Hamiltonians, two basic problems in quantum complexity theory. The authors present faster exponential quantum algorithms whose runtime exponent is governed by the binary entropy function. Their main technical result is an entropy-governed lower bound on the dimension of the Hamiltonian's low-energy subspace, obtained by depolarizing the ground state, which is optimal up to constant factors in the exponent for fixed k. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present an entropy-governed lower bound on low-energy subspace dimension, improving exponents for k-local Hamiltonian algorithms; they report it is near-optimal for fixed k and give tighte

entry.title: QBX: A Compiler for Simulating 2-local Qubit Hamiltonians on Quantum Chiplets
entry.summary: QBX: A Compiler for 2-local Qubit Hamiltonian Simulation on Quantum Chiplets arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper presents QBX, the first quantum compiler built for simulating 2-local qubit Hamiltonians on quantum chiplet architectures. It uses a scalable hierarchical approach and a highway mechanism to reduce the number and distance of cross-chiplet communications. According to the authors' evaluations, QBX outperforms both general-purpose and domain-specific compilers in circuit depth and operation count, and scales to larger simulations.

entry.title: Autonomous phase discovery: a paper on automatically exploring quantum phases with differentiable programming and unsupervised learning
entry.summary: Autonomous phase discovery arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper introduces a fully autonomous system that combines differentiable programming and unsupervised learning to discover quantum phases of matter without phase labels or a prescribed target phase. The search evaluates ground-state data along an adaptive trajectory rather than a fixed parameter grid. On a generalized cluster chain with up to 200 distinct phases, it finds up to 25 more phases at the same budget and matches random sampling given thirty times its budget. On a 50-parameter Chern insulator, it reaches sectors that the simple harmonic constructions considered do not obtain. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a fully autonomous system combining differentiable programming and unsupervised learning to find quantum phases along adaptive trajectories; the authors report up to 25 more phases than rando

entry.title: Certifying finite-measurement learning of multiscale quantum states
entry.summary: Terminal-Register Certification for Finite-Measurement Learning of Multiscale Quantum States arXiv · Sep 27, 2026This paper studies reliable learning of pure one-dimensional quantum states from finite measurements, using an inverse binary multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA). The authors add a noise-aware theorem that includes a calibrated total variation implementation budget in the finite-shot certificate. On a transverse field Ising ground state, an 8-qubit schedule exceeded fidelity 0.99 in all 60 held-out runs, with mean fidelity 0.996886. At 16 qubits, MERA outperformed a parameter-matched local circuit in fidelity and long-range error.

entry.title: Testing a Conjecture on Entangled Qubit Noise: A Twenty-Year Review
entry.summary: The Fully Depolarizing Noise Conjecture for Entangled Physical States: A Twenty-Year Perspective arXiv · Sep 27, 2026The author revisits a 2006 conjecture that noise acting on entangled physical qubits includes a joint fully depolarizing component, which could obstruct quantum fault tolerance. The conjecture remains open, but recent experimental advances bring it closer to empirical testing on current devices. The paper also discusses noise sensitivity and complexity in noisy intermediate-scale quantum systems, and statistical analysis of quantum advantage claims.

entry.title: Diffusive spectral gap of the qubit eSWAP chain
entry.summary: The diffusive spectral gap of the qubit eSWAP chain arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper proves that the second-moment Hamiltonian of the open qubit eSWAP chain has a diffusive spectral gap, resolving a conjecture by Li, Zheng, Liu, Jiang, and Liu. It characterises the ground space on connected interaction graphs with at least five vertices and gives a uniform lower bound for the unnormalised complete-graph gap. These results are applied to sequential and brickwork circuits, and the periodic chain is shown to also have a diffusive spectral gap. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that the open qubit eSWAP chain's second-moment Hamiltonian has a diffusive spectral gap, resolving a conjecture of Li et al. They also characterise the ground space on connected gra

entry.title: Heisenberg-limited spin squeezing in multi-level spins, protected by local interactions
entry.summary: Gap-Protected Heisenberg-Limited Squeezing with Locally Interacting Multi-Level Spins arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper proposes a general way to create entanglement useful for metrology, called generalized spin squeezing, in multi-level (qudit) spin systems with power-law interactions. It extends spin-nematic squeezing from spinor BECs to spatially extended lattices. Without all-to-all connectivity, dynamics leak into non-collective modes and lose Heisenberg scaling. Adding local su(D) exchange interactions opens an energy gap that protects the symmetric collective manifold, achieving ξ²∝1/N scaling in one to three dimensions.

entry.title: A quantum algorithm for solving Riccati equations, with near-optimal complexity analysis
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithm and Complexity Analysis for Riccati Problems arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper develops quantum algorithms that build block-encodings of solution matrices for algebraic, differential, and finite-horizon Riccati problems. A unified Quantum Weighted Riesz Method is used, and under stated assumptions the algebraic cases achieve near-optimal query complexity up to logarithmic factors. The authors also prove lower bounds and BQP-completeness results for certain promise problems. Applications include linear-quadratic control, quantum chemistry, and heated boundary control with numerical validation. ★★★★ Notable: A weighted Riesz quantum method unifies four Riccati problem types; the authors give near-optimal query bounds, product lower bounds, and BQP-completeness for selected-value problems, with limited num

entry.title: Transient heat conduction on quantum hardware: a variational solver's temperature-field accuracy and shot-count limits
entry.summary: Transient Heat Conduction on Quantum Hardware: Replicated Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Shot-Count Sensitivity with a Variational Quantum Linear Solver arXiv · Oct 16, 2026The paper tests a variational quantum linear solver (VQLS) on IBM quantum hardware, solving one backward-Euler step of one-dimensional heat conduction. A confirmatory comparison of N=4 and N=8 temperatures shows larger field error on hardware for N=8. An exploratory N=16 case and a shot-count follow-up show that increasing shots reduces variability but does not recover the mean cold-side temperature field.

entry.title: Nonlinear quantum spin dynamics without entanglement: a variational method extending classical atomistic spin dynamics to quantum spins
entry.summary: Nonlinear quantum multi-spin dynamics without entanglement arXiv · Oct 5, 2026The paper proposes a variational product-state framework that extends classical atomistic spin dynamics to quantum spins of arbitrary size s, allowing both pure and mixed local states. It excludes intersite entanglement while retaining local quantum effects from the nonclassical structure of density operators for s≥1. The authors analyze why quantum Landau-Lifshitz and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics are inequivalent and when they match under a common time rescaling, and they note that the method allows O(N) simulations of spin dynamics in materials.

entry.title: Adaptive filtering for qubit readout tests whether extra processing improves state discrimination
entry.summary: Real-Time Adaptive Filtering and the Boxcar Limit in Superconducting Qubit Readout arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper examines when extra digital processing improves readout fidelity in superconducting qubit systems. It compares a real-time adaptive FIR filter trained with LMS on an FPGA against the standard boxcar averager, using both live hardware and offline analysis of measured shots. For the fixed filters tested, the filtered sum reduces to the boxcar sum times a complex number, so discrimination did not improve, though the frozen LMS filter reduced trace noise. Changing the decision method cut labeled shots per state by 89.8% on a 3D ancilla readout and assigned most shots before the window ended.

entry.title: Quantum-classical break-even for electronic dynamics of large ring molecules
entry.summary: Quantum--classical break-even in electronic dynamics of macrocyclic molecules arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper shows that quantum hardware can reach useful accuracy in chemical dynamics simulations within wall-clock times comparable to estimated practical classical computing. The authors target ring-shaped conjugated macrocycles such as benzene and [60]annulene, compressing short-time evolution with tensor networks and replicating the circuit using rotational symmetry. On IBM quantum processors, a hybrid approach was compared against two state-of-the-art classical methods, finding comparable accuracy and computational time under ideal parallelization.

entry.title: Limits of adaptive two-way linear postprocessing in six-state quantum key distribution
entry.summary: Limits of adaptive two-way linear postprocessing in six-state quantum key distribution arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper studies how far adaptive linear postprocessing with two-way classical communication can improve noise tolerance in six-state quantum key distribution. The authors construct a single compatible collective attack that defeats a broad class of linear postprocessing. They prove that Eve's optimal probability of recovering any linear function of Alice's raw key is at least Bob's, so reliable agreement on a linear final key is incompatible with secrecy. ★★★★ Notable: The paper constructs a single compatible collective attack for six-state QKD, arguing that adaptive linear postprocessing cannot simultaneously achieve reliable agreement and secrecy over a range of e

entry.title: Analyzing quantum circuit fault tolerance with tensor networks and symplectic geometry
entry.summary: Fault tolerance of quantum circuits with tensor networks and symplectic geometry arXiv · Oct 3, 2026The paper presents an operator-algebraic framework for analyzing fault tolerance in quantum circuits, giving necessary and sufficient conditions for exact recovery of the ideal computation under a given noise model. For non-adaptive stabilizer circuits, it uses symplectic geometry to derive closed-form detection and logical-effect matrices that characterize circuit distance. Applied to a finite Hastings–Haah honeycomb Floquet-code circuit, these matrices certify two logical qubits with distance four, and linear programming yields upper bounds on circuit distance. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an operator-algebraic and symplectic framework giving an SDP test and LP distance bounds, checked on Floquet and Hamming codes.

entry.title: Trapping nanofabricated silicon dioxide discs in an optical lattice for sensing
entry.summary: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO₂ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper describes fabricating 10-micrometer-diameter, 400-nanometer-thick silicon dioxide discs and loading them into a vacuum optical standing-wave trap. The authors combine interferometric and imaging methods to measure the center-of-mass motional spectra of the discs. The approach supports efficient loading and trapping of only a few particles with customizable geometries compatible with wafer-scale nanofabrication. Disc-like trapped particles are identified as promising for high-frequency gravitational-wave detectors or sensitive accelerometers.

entry.title: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries: a method for building and solving such theories on finite intervals
entry.summary: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries arXiv · Oct 3, 2026The paper presents a general method to construct and solve time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on finite intervals, starting from autonomous scattering and reflection data. It derives boundary quantum Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov equations, with local and global consistency ensured by the Yang–Baxter and reflection equations and boundary-qKZ flatness, and reconstructs the local Hamiltonian via Cayley inversion. The construction is applied to rational SU(N) scattering with boundary impurities and to an O(3) model with a spin-1/2 impurity. For the SU(2) impurity, explicit boundary-qKZ solutions are given, recovering static open-chain Bethe equations when the drive rate vanishes.

entry.title: How many copies are needed to estimate quantum state moments, and why third and fourth moments are equally hard
entry.summary: Optimal single-copy estimation of quantum state moments: why Tr(ρ³⁾ and Tr(ρ⁴⁾ are equally hard arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper studies how many single-copy measurements are needed to estimate the moments Tr(ρ^t) of an unknown quantum state. For each fixed integer t≥2 it gives matching upper and lower bounds on the optimal sample complexity. The exponent follows a dyadic pattern, so the third and fourth moments both require Θ(d^{2/3}) copies. ★★★★ Notable: The paper gives the optimal single-copy sample complexity for estimating Tr(ρ^t), showing a dyadic hierarchy where t=3 and t=4 both need Θ(d^{2/3}) copies; the upper bound uses adaptive state filterin

entry.title: Exact distances and measurement allocation for logical Pauli readout (how many measurements a fault-tolerant logical readout needs)
entry.summary: Exact distances and measurement allocation for logical Pauli readout arXiv · Oct 3, 2026This paper studies how the minimum fault weight of a logical Pauli readout depends on data-error persistence, check redundancy, and time-boundary constraints. It proves an exact distance formula for a repeated-readout model and gives the minimum repetition count needed for each adjacent-column check in square Bacon-Shor and generalized Shor readouts. Combining these with redundant Gauss-check pair products yields an exact joint distance and an optimal outcome count within the specified gauged-readout family.

entry.title: A two-part quantum-classical universe in which ħ emerges from classical time
entry.summary: The quantum-classical bipartite universe and the logical emergence of hbar from classical temporality arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper reinterprets quantum dynamics within the standard von Neumann formalism, proposing a logical split between a classical observing environment governed by Boolean logic and a quantum observed system governed by non-Boolean logic. It models an ideal classical clock as an open system with uniformly discretized energy levels, described by the GKSL master equation. The author derives the reduced Planck constant ħ as a scaling parameter from the clock's action operator and claims an exact mapping to 't Hooft's cellular automaton formalism.

entry.title: Coherent release fronts in Krylov chains and thermal AdS2 response
entry.summary: Coherent Release Fronts in Krylov Chains and Thermal AdS₂ Response arXiv · Oct 2, 2026The paper studies coherent release from a finite serial Krylov sector into an exact conformal tail with asymptotically linear Lanczos coefficients. It derives the cumulative occupation behind a front that moves to greater Krylov depth over time. The tail sets the logarithmic transit scale while the finite sector shapes the distribution. The framework is illustrated in thermal AdS2, where weak coupling yields a two-site shallow sector coupled to the conformal tail.

entry.title: Unified algebraic theory of spacetime quantum fault tolerance
entry.summary: Theory of spacetime quantum fault tolerance arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper presents a unified algebraic theory of Clifford spacetime quantum fault tolerance, which supports universal fault-tolerant quantum computation. The authors build a spacetime chain complex from a circuit's tensor network representation, describing fault propagation, detector syndromes, and logical actions. The framework unifies spacetime codes, Gottesman's gadget framework, fault complexes, and ZX calculus, and accommodates phenomenological and circuit-level fault models.

entry.title: Testing Quantum Control Circuits Simultaneously with Finite Reversible Models
entry.summary: Simultaneous Circuit Tests for Finite Reversible Models of Quantum Control arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper studies whether one finite reversible model can reproduce the probabilities of a whole collection of quantum circuits at once, using a shared transition table. It gives an exact feasibility formulation and a 464-frame benchmark showing a sharp repeated-circuit horizon: one controller stays within error 1/3 through 192 blocks, while every allowed controller violates it by block 193. The conclusions apply only to the stated finite reversible model classes and do not establish a universal memory bound or a discrepancy for physical hardware.

entry.title: Stationarity as a one-mode constraint on quantum correlation
entry.summary: Stationarity as a One-Mode Constraint on Quantum Correlation arXiv · Oct 2, 2026The paper argues that a stationary scalar correlation energy admits an exact one-mode terminal representation even when the microscopic correlated response is strongly multimode. The authors test predictive realizations built from specified stationary information carriers in two-electron systems, He-like ions and harmonium, which share Coulomb repulsion but differ in confinement. Results show small correlation-energy errors for the Coulomb sequence, a validity limit at H⁻, and agreement with reference values for harmonic confinement at larger frequencies.

entry.title: Pruning Quantum Circuits to Cut Unnecessary Two-Qubit Gates Across Hardware Types
entry.summary: Quantum Circuit Pruning: From NISQ Architectures to Fault-Tolerant Operations arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper proposes a routing-aware pruning method that removes parametric two-qubit gates when their fidelity cost outweighs their computational contribution. The approach is evaluated on both NISQ and fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures. In NISQ simulations on benchmark circuits, gate count fell by up to 48.6% and fidelity improved by up to 47.7%. A feasibility analysis suggests pruning remains relevant on fault-tolerant hardware across a range of code distances and physical error rates.

entry.title: A two-stage quantum-classical method for reconfiguring distribution networks using cycle-edge encoding
entry.summary: Two-Stage Quantum-Classical Distribution Network Reconfiguration via Cycle-Edge Encoding arXiv · Oct 1, 2026The paper proposes a two-stage method combining quantum and classical computing to reconfigure electrical distribution networks for lower losses. A quantum search, using an iterative linear-ramp QAOA over subspaces built with a cycle-edge encoding that guarantees spanning-tree configurations, produces samples that guide a mixed-integer second-order-cone solver. It is tested on six networks of 33 to 417 buses using simulation and trapped-ion quantum hardware. For the 417-bus network, hardware sampling finds a configuration within about 1.4% of the literature reference loss.

entry.title: Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Is Fermionic Magic
entry.summary: Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Is Fermionic Magic arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper shows that free fermion dynamics is classically simulable and that a single non-Gaussian state makes it universal, and that the same boundary governs quantum nonlocality. Such maps are uniformly approximated by Wigner symmetries, with error at most 9ε/2 in trace distance and 2√2ε in Bures distance. entry.title: Exchange-controlled quantum beats and entanglement in an exciton–bimodal-cavity system
entry.summary: Exchange-controlled quantum beats and entanglement in an exciton--bimodal-cavity system arXiv · Oct 3, 2026This theoretical paper studies two excitons coupled to a bimodal optical cavity, including an exciton-exciton exchange interaction, showing tunable population transfer and entanglement generation. Parameterized with first-principles data for graphene nanoribbon excitons, it finds that in the large-exchange regime nearly complete transfer between excitonic states occurs over many coherent cycles. The authors provide analytical design rules linking beat period, transfer amplitude and coherent-cycle number to exchange, cavity detuning and light–matter coupling.

entry.title: Exact Timing of Entanglement and Negativity Criticalities in Open Fermion Chains
entry.summary: Exact Temporal Criticalities of Entanglement and Negativity in Gaussian and Non-Gaussian Dissipative Kitaev Chains arXiv · Oct 3, 2026This paper studies when the two largest eigenvalues of entanglement and negativity spectra in open fermionic systems, including Kitaev chains, become degenerate, closing the gap of the corresponding Hamiltonian while entropies remain smooth. The authors call this a temporal criticality and compare Gaussian loss and gain with non-Gaussian density dephasing. They find that Gaussianity, rather than the symmetry type, determines the criterion for criticality. Exact solutions are given at a point where the chain's bond terms commute, showing how dephasing shifts the criticalities.

entry.title: Adding a single photon to multimode quantum light in lithium niobate crystals at telecom wavelengths
entry.summary: Single-photon addition to multimode quantum fields at telecom wavelengths using lithium niobate and its doped variants arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper presents a theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of single-photon addition (SPA) and mode-selective single-photon addition (MSSPA) to multimode quantum fields at telecom wavelengths. The study covers congruent lithium niobate, 5% MgO-doped lithium niobate, and various concentrations of ZnO-doped lithium niobate crystals. It also examines spectro-temporal mode-selective SPA over temperatures from 0°C to 15°C and identifies phase-matching parameters for non-Gaussian state engineering, mainly at 1550 nm.

entry.title: A mentor-led two-way teleportation protocol that handles any qubit state
entry.summary: Mentor-Initiated Asymmetric Bidirectional Quantum Teleportation Protocol for Arbitrary Qubit States arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper proposes a bidirectional asymmetric quantum teleportation protocol initiated by a mentor. Existing schemes limit the two-qubit state sent from Bob to Alice to a Bell-like form, whereas this protocol allows an arbitrary two-qubit state to be teleported in the same framework. The required entangled resources are built from standard quantum gates, and the protocol is implemented as a quantum circuit and simulated in Qiskit. The simulated probability distributions for the chosen input states are very close to the theoretical values.

entry.title: Complexity of the Hartle-Hawking state in JT gravity, measured by Wigner negativity
entry.summary: Complexity study of the Hartle-Hawking state in JT gravity arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper studies how the negativity of the Wigner function of the Hartle-Hawking state in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity grows under time evolution. Wigner negativity is presented as a measure of how hard the quantum state is to simulate on a classical computer. At genus zero and high temperature, the leading-order state is a minimum-uncertainty Gaussian wavepacket at rest at the Liouville wall turning point, with a positive Wigner function. Numerical results show late-time negativity approaching a value consistent with 0.08 e^{-4.4/β}, larger at lower temperature.

entry.title: ALPS Project 3.0: open-source software for simulating strongly correlated quantum systems
entry.summary: The ALPS project release 3.0: open source software for strongly correlated systems arXiv · Oct 3, 2026ALPS is an open-source project providing libraries and programs for simulating strongly correlated quantum lattice models, such as quantum magnets and lattice bosons. Release 3.0 adds distribution via pip and Spack, moves development to GitHub with continuous integration, switches to the MIT license, and rebuilds documentation and tutorials. It also modernizes the C++ codebase, updates the DMRG code, and removes legacy components.

entry.title: Complete proof that weighted gapped clique homology is QMA₁-hard
entry.summary: A Complete Proof of mathsfQMA₁-Hardness for Weighted Gapped Clique Homology arXiv · Oct 3, 2026This paper studies the computational complexity of simplicial homology and proves that the weighted, spectrally gapped version of clique homology is QMA₁-hard. entry.title: Level-3 quantum bootstrap is not tight for a 3D double well at an excited level
entry.summary: Strict non-tightness of the level-3 quantum bootstrap for a natural three-dimensional Hamiltonian, at an excited level arXiv · Oct 2, 2026The paper studies the coupled three-dimensional double-well Hamiltonian and constructs, at the first excited level and at the ground state, a linear functional on polynomials of degree at most 6. entry.title: Beyond Pure Dephasing: Why Single-Molecule Quantum Error Correction Needs Multiple Spins
entry.summary: Beyond Pure Dephasing: Quantum Error Correction in Single Molecules Requires Multiple Spins arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper proposes multi-spin molecules as a possible architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing. It introduces a correction protocol that handles both diagonal errors (dephasing) and off-diagonal errors (relaxation) using a hybrid encoding. The scheme first suppresses the leading pure dephasing error, then uses a multi-qubit code within a multi-spin molecule for the remaining off-diagonal errors. Numerical results indicate the approach may perform well even with a limited number of spins per logical unit.

entry.title: From static Lindblad stabilizability to robust physical control sequences
entry.summary: From Static Lindblad Stabilizability to Robust Physical Control Sequences arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper studies how dissipative dynamics can stabilize a quantum state at a target, even when the available finite control operations are imperfect. The authors derive checkable conditions that bound convergence, errors during operations, and physical cost, covering pulses, idle intervals, and background dynamics. They also present a finite-library search that yields a control sequence for a specified four-level cascade model, with an explicit preparation-time bound.

entry.title: Emergent quantum geometric phases in patterned graphene that mimic moiré electronic states
entry.summary: Emergent Quantum Geometric Phases in Holey Graphene arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The authors fabricate encapsulated monolayer graphene with patterned periodic antidot lattices and measure its magnetotransport. Tuning the lattice size reveals classical commensurability features from cyclotron orbits of similar radii, along with Brown-Zak oscillations from quantum commensurability between the magnetic flux quantum and the lattice unit cell. The paper reports that the system's geometric phase is directly measurable and that lithographic patterning can generate moiré-like spectra without twisting or stacking layers.

entry.title: Multipartite entanglement hidden in spin-chain vector-chiral correlations
entry.summary: Multipartite entanglement hidden in vector-chiral correlations of spin-1/2 chains arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper derives a rigorous entanglement bound for the total nearest-neighbour vector chirality of periodic spin-1/2 chains with an even number of sites. Exceeding the bound on quantum Fisher information per spin certifies an entanglement depth of at least k+1. Using infinite DMRG and thermal pure quantum-state calculations, the authors show multipartite entanglement in vector-chiral correlations at zero and finite temperatures in an extended J1-J2 XXZ chain.

entry.title: An operational characterization of finite-dimensional quantum theory
entry.summary: An operational characterization of finite-dimensional quantum theory arXiv · Oct 3, 2026The paper constructs a finite set of two-body correlations such that the only probabilistic theory that realizes them and stays stable under iterated teleportation is quantum theory. For n systems of dimension d, the first condition can be checked with poly(d,n) measurement settings. The second condition is a hierarchy of tests, one per teleportation step count N, so finite-dimensional quantum theory can be self-tested. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes uniquely characterizing finite-dimensional quantum theory using finitely many two-body correlations plus stability under iterated teleportation. entry.title: Layer codes as quantum memories: a 3D error-correcting code tested for syndrome extraction, thresholds and idle robustness
entry.summary: Layer codes as quantum memories: syndrome extraction, thresholds and idle robustness arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper evaluates layer codes, three-dimensional local CSS codes built from unrotated surface code patches, as active quantum memories under circuit-level noise. The authors present a decoder-free scheduler for syndrome extraction circuits and compare eighteen layer codes with surface codes of the same distance. A primary family built from a [[4,2,2]] input code reaches a circuit-level threshold of 5.06(7)×10^-3. The layer codes tolerate 1.7 to 3.0 times longer intervals between syndrome extraction rounds than rotated surface codes, at the cost of more operations per unit time and about five times more physical qubits per logical qubit.

entry.title: Square-root growth of operator entanglement in an integrable circuit
entry.summary: Square-root growth of operator entanglement in an integrable brickwork circuit arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper builds a four-state brickwork circuit whose gate is a permutation matrix solving the constant Yang-Baxter equation, as a counterexample to the expected logarithmic growth of operator entanglement. Matrix product operator simulations at fixed error below one need bond dimension growing at least exponentially in the square root of time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a counterexample in an integrable four-state brickwork circuit, reporting square-root growth of operator von Neumann entanglement and an exponential lower bound on the MPO bond dimen

entry.title: A numerical, efficient model for thermo-field electron emission calculations (GETELEC-3)
entry.summary: A numerical and efficient model for thermo-field electron emission calculations arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper presents GETELEC-3, an open-source code that replaces analytical thermo-field emission formulas, such as Fowler-Nordheim and Murphy-Good with their JWKB extensions, with a direct numerical solution of the one-dimensional time-independent Schrödinger equation. The Numerov algorithm was found to be the fastest method, with solution uncertainty below 1%. A neural network trained on the residual of the semiclassical reference reproduces the current density to better than 0.4% at lower computational cost. The code targets metals and semiconductors and accepts arbitrary potentials and densities of states.

entry.title: Exact unitary synthesis with optimal circuit size and depth-ancilla tradeoff
entry.summary: Exact Unitary Synthesis: Simultaneously Optimal in Size and Depth-Ancilla Tradeoff arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper studies how to exactly decompose an arbitrary n-qubit unitary into elementary quantum gates. For any ancilla budget m, the authors build a circuit of O(4^n) CNOT and single-qubit gates arranged in O(n+4^n/(n+m)) layers. This matches the asymptotically optimal depth-ancilla tradeoff and optimal circuit size at once. The method encodes basis states as wavefunctions with a shared Gaussian envelope, discretizes the result, and removes approximation errors through exact residual correction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors encode basis states as wavefunctions sharing a Gaussian envelope, turning unitary action into coordinate transformations, and report exact synthesis with O(4^n) size and O(n+4^n/(n+m)) dep

entry.title: Neural correlation learning for quantum-enhanced sensing with time-independently driven Rydberg atom arrays
entry.summary: Neural Correlation Learning for Quantum-Enhanced Sensing with Time-Independently Driven Rydberg Atom Arrays arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper shows that evolving a simple product state under time-independent Hamiltonian dynamics in Rydberg atom arrays creates many-body correlations that could enable quantum-enhanced parameter estimation approaching the Heisenberg limit. The authors propose a neural correlation learning framework combining Bayesian inference with neural networks trained on calibration data, used in a two-stage calibration-and-sensing protocol. Numerical results indicate it saturates the Cramér–Rao bound set by the classical Fisher information, surpassing the standard quantum limit, and remains robust to realistic noise.

entry.title: Verifying quantum error-correcting code parameters with short, provably sized certificates
entry.summary: Quantum error-correcting code parameters, checkable by a certificate of provable size arXiv · Oct 2, 2026Quantum error-correcting codes are described by physical qubit count, logical qubit count, and distance, and the distance is usually obtained from a solver. This paper shows that code parameters can be certified by short certificates whose correctness a proof assistant's kernel checks by computation, with certificate size itself proved as a theorem. The authors settle distances for two published code families and report results for eleven code families and thirty-nine parameter sets. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes short certificates, checkable by a proof assistant kernel, for quantum code parameters; the abstract reports settling distances of two published families across eleven families and thirty-nin

entry.title: Metastability of the Mean-Field Interchange Model for Local Dimension ≥3
entry.summary: On the Metastability of the Mean-Field Interchange Model for Local Dimension ≥ 3 arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper studies how quantum systems thermalize at low temperatures. The authors show that the Davies dynamics of a mean-field interchange model with local dimension d≥3 and single-site generalized Pauli couplings has two distinguished inverse temperatures, with a static first-order phase transition between them. Between these temperatures, the spectral gap of the Davies generator vanishes exponentially in system size n, indicating metastability. Outside this interval, the gap is bounded below by an inverse polynomial in n, allowing polynomial-time thermalization.

entry.title: Proposed matter-wave interferometer using a rare-earth-doped microparticle
entry.summary: Proposal for matter-wave interferometry with a rare-earth-doped microparticle arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper proposes demonstrating matter-wave interference with a microparticle containing an embedded rare-earth ion. Optical transitions of the ion impart momentum to the particle's center of mass, and a time-symmetric geometry with J = 1/2 is used to remove sensitivity to initial conditions. The authors argue that external decoherence rates either decrease or stay constant as particle mass increases, so larger particles can avoid decoherence.

entry.title: Spin-orbit-induced gauge field and spin Hall effects in light fluids
entry.summary: Spin-orbit-induced gauge field and spin Hall effects in quasi-paraxial fluids of light arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper studies quasi-paraxial light fluids propagating in nonlinear Kerr media. The authors show that intrinsic spin-orbit interaction of light, encoded in Maxwell's equations, produces an effective gauge field whose sign depends on helicity and magnitude on nonlinear refractive index variations. Its effects are illustrated for flow past an obstacle and for the cumulative precession of a wave packet in a focusing fluid.

entry.title: A perturbative framework for non-Gaussian, nonunitary environments with nonlinear coupling
entry.summary: Game of Nons: Non-Gaussian Nonunitary Environments with Nonlinear Coupling arXiv · Oct 5, 2026The paper presents a perturbative framework for systems quadratically coupled to bosonic environments, which may be single- or multimode and have non-Gaussian, nonstationary initial states. Using linear evolution in a doubled operator space and a characteristic-function representation, it expresses ordered multitime environmental correlation functions via derivatives of the initial characteristic function. These correlators are used to recursively build the time-convolutionless generator at any finite order. A qubit coupled to a damped mode through a two-photon interaction serves as an illustrative example.

entry.title: Performance of Multiparty GHZ-State Quantum Conference Key Agreement over Optical Fiber
entry.summary: Performance Analysis of Multiparty GHZ-State Quantum Conference Key Agreement over Optical Fiber Channel arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper studies the finite-key performance of a multiparty quantum conference key agreement system that distributes GHZ states over optical fiber. Each link is modeled as an erasure-Pauli channel extended with detector dark counts, and closed-form error-rate expressions are derived. The local bit-error rate depends only on transmissivity and dark counts, while the global phase-error rate accumulates across links and degrades faster with distance and more parties. Optimizing the parameter-estimation probability raises the secret-key rate and extends the maximum secure distance.

entry.title: Correspondence between walks and zeta functions for quantum walks on path graphs, a pre-geometric structure from a generalized reflection principle
entry.summary: Walk/Zeta correspondence for quantum walks on path graphs: a pre-geometric structure implied by a generalized reflection principle arXiv · Oct 5, 2026The paper establishes a local Konno-Sato correspondence for reflected random and Szegedy walks on a finite path graph. A generalized reflection principle using explicit involutions yields exact zeta factorizations into a boundary factor and local factors indexed by the infinite dihedral group. After symmetrization, classical and quantum local factors correspond for each group element, and the identity contribution determines the normalized thermodynamic limits. Under a double scaling of asymmetry and spectral parameter, the quantum factorization yields a massive Dirac-type limit.

entry.summary: Shallow Quantum Circuits for Geometrically Local Lindblad Dynamics arXiv · Oct 5, 2026The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for simulating time-independent, finite-range Lindblad (open quantum system) dynamics on a lattice, allowing noncommuting jump operators. entry.title: Lifted surgery for non-Abelian two-block group-algebra codes
entry.summary: Lifted surgery for non-Abelian two-block group-algebra codes arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper extends lifted code surgery, a method that measures logical operators of quantum LDPC codes using a merged code, from Abelian to non-Abelian two-block group-algebra codes. The authors classify the block-affine automorphisms of these codes and find that most apparent non-Abelian gains vanish when measured against the full symmetry group. They prove the gain is at most the index of a largest Abelian subgroup, and report codes and circuit-level simulations with Relay-BP decoding in which the non-Abelian gadget is as reliable as the Abelian gadgets while using two to three times fewer rounds.

entry.title: A structured AI-agent workflow for applied quantum computing research, with a worked chemistry example
entry.summary: Demonstration of a Structured Agentic Workflow for Applied Quantum Computing Research arXiv · Oct 5, 2026The paper introduces the Quantum Agentic Operating System (QAOS), a structured multi-agent system for quantum and computational research projects that splits work into constrained, sandboxed tasks. It is demonstrated on a quantum chemistry prototyping task: modeling a proton-transfer problem using sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), with FCI and DFT as classical references. entry.title: Faster randomized compilers for simulating open quantum systems under Lindblad dynamics
entry.summary: Fast Random Compilers for Time-Dependent and Time-Independent Lindbladian Simulation arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper develops first- and second-order randomized sampling algorithms for simulating Lindbladian dynamics, covering both time-independent and time-dependent cases. For time-independent Lindbladians, the second-order correction improves the precision dependence from ε^-1 to ε^-1/2 in the number of time slices. Because the second-order maps need not be CPTP, they are used to estimate observable expectation values rather than to prepare output states deterministically.

entry.title: Quantum n-coloring is undecidable for every n ≥ 3
entry.summary: Quantum n-coloring is undecidable for every n ≥ 3 arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper studies the quantum n-coloring problem, which asks whether a graph G has a perfect quantum strategy for its n-coloring game. Previously, undecidability was known only for n=3. The authors extend this to all n≥3 using one elementary reduction. They define G'=(G□K3)∨K(n−3) and show that G is quantum 3-colorable if and only if G' is quantum n-colorable.

entry.title: Origin and classification of fractional dynamical topology in non-Hermitian quantum systems
entry.summary: Origin and classification of fractional dynamical topology in non-Hermitian quantum systems arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper studies dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPT) in non-Hermitian quantum systems. In a two-band non-Hermitian model, the authors show that half-integer jumps of the dynamical topological order parameter originate from discontinuities in the complex energy spectrum. This behavior is linked to the steady-state phase diagram of the quench Hamiltonian, and the occurrence of DQPT is classified. The analysis is extended to multiband and two-dimensional models.

entry.title: Complete classification of reversible entanglement conversions between two-qutrit states
entry.summary: Complete Classification of Reversible Entanglement Transformations of Two Qutrits arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper studies when two parties, Alice and Bob, can convert two-qutrit mixed states into one another and back using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). It gives a complete classification of such reversible conversions. For mutually convertible entangled states that are not locally unitarily equivalent, it proves a decomposition into a separable part and an entangled block is necessary. Two entangled states are reversibly convertible if and only if their unnormalized smallest retained blocks are locally unitarily equivalent. ★★★★ Notable: Gives a complete classification of reversible two-qutrit LOCC conversions with a minimal retained block; strong theory, but impact is confined to a narrow quantum information niche.

entry.summary: Efficient Fidelity Estimation of General Quantum Resource States via Clifford Circuits arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper introduces Bell-coherence fidelity estimation (BCFE), a method for estimating the fidelity of quantum resource states using only Clifford gates and Pauli measurements. entry.title: Radio-frequency electron cascade in semiconductor quantum dots
entry.summary: Radio-frequency electron cascade in semiconductor quantum dots arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper studies radio-frequency (rf)-driven correlated cotunneling in semiconductor quantum dots, where electrons move simultaneously across multiple tunnel junctions via virtual intermediate states. Using theory and experiments on two foundry-fabricated silicon devices, the authors show that an rf drive induces correlated cyclic single-electron transitions that enhance charge polarization. They present a general framework for rf electron-cascade readout using three or more dots and demonstrate it in a gate-sensed architecture, aiming to improve dispersive readout fidelity.

entry.title: Universal convergence of standard quantum electrodynamics to the modified Langevin noise formalism
entry.summary: Universal and rigorous asymptotic convergence of standard macroscopic quantum electrodynamics to the modified Langevin noise formalism arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper examines whether the standard Langevin noise formalism (LNF), which adds fictitious vacuum absorption that vanishes in a limit, reproduces every prediction of the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF), including quantum scattering processes. entry.title: Error-transparent switching between two permutation-invariant quantum codes
entry.summary: Error-Transparent Code Switching Between Permutation-Invariant Codes with Transversal Clifford and Icosahedral Gates arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper studies moving an encoded qubit between two permutation-invariant codes on the same qubits, one supporting transversal Clifford gates and the other transversal gates from the binary icosahedral group. The authors show that distance-three codes with the required properties are cut out by at most two quadratic equations, and that a single-fault-tolerant switch exists exactly when the codes are joined by a continuous path of such codes. On thirteen qubits they construct the switching unitary along an explicit circle and numerically verify machine-precision recovery infidelity per fault.

entry.title: Completeness of Quantum Mechanics: Sources, Records, and Probabilities
entry.summary: On the Completeness of Quantum Mechanics: Sources, Records and Probabilities arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper asks whether quantum mechanics can be complete without being fundamental. Under stated source, detector, and statistical conditions, the authors reconstruct the quantum representation and Born probabilities and prove algebraic closure of the admitted predictions without a collapse postulate. They argue that many familiar quantum paradoxes arise from conflating coherent processes with retained records, or probabilities with realized outcomes.

entry.title: How much non-Gaussian resource fermionic randomness needs for quantum sampling
entry.summary: The magic cost of fermionic randomness arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper asks how much non-Gaussianity is needed for sampling-based quantum advantage to reproduce random-matrix statistics linked to quantum chaos. It shows that passive fermionic linear optics, even with Haar-random mode mixing, fails to anticoncentrate for Slater inputs. entry.title: JAQSI: A Differentiable Quantum Simulator Unifying Gate- and Pulse-Level Simulation
entry.summary: JAQSI: Just Another Quantum Simulator arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper presents JAQSI, a quantum simulator built on JAX that combines gate-level and pulse-level simulation in one differentiable circuit model. It allows matrix-defined operations, gates synthesised from Hamiltonian evolution, and noise channels to be composed freely. In benchmarks against PennyLane, Qiskit, Qibo, Qulacs, QuTiP and dynamiqs, the authors report performance on par with or up to an order of magnitude faster at the gate level, and at least 5 times faster in pulse-level benchmarks. The software is released as open source on GitHub and PyPI.

entry.title: Phase-controlled recoverable entanglement in accelerated detector registers
entry.summary: Phase-controlled recoverable entanglement in accelerated detector registers arXiv · Oct 4, 2026This paper studies recoverable entanglement in a four-qubit cluster-state register whose two detector qubits couple to a scalar field. A local preparation phase controls protection under collective noise, and at the optimal phase a fixed decoder recovers a Bell pair after channels preserving singlet and triplet sectors. The authors derive an exact trace-norm formula for uniformly accelerated detectors and the decay rate at small separation.

entry.title: Quantum Fisher-Selke sequence in a transverse-field Ising model and its bilayer
entry.summary: Onset of a quantum Fisher-Selke sequence in the transverse-field ANNNI model and its bilayer arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper studies a transverse-field Ising model with next-nearest-neighbor coupling on a square lattice and a bilayer. Perturbation theory in the transverse field, carried to eighth order, shows that quantum fluctuations select a three-up-three-down phase first, followed by further phases in the order of the classical Fisher-Selke sequence. Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the two widest phases largely support these results.
